pages.title: Help - Settings: Player
pages.description: Player holds the settings for viewing and playing your files: default order, slideshow timing, what you may do to a file while viewing it, player controls, touch zones and background audio.
pages.body: Help index / Settings: Player Settings: Player What this is for Player holds the settings for viewing and playing your files: default order, slideshow timing, what you may do to a file while viewing it, player controls, touch zones and background audio. In this order There is no fixed order here - every option works on its own. They are grouped below by the same section headers you see on the tab. The elements Sorting, slideshow and playback order 1 Default sort mode Sets the default order of files. Choose manual order, or sort by name, date, size or type, each ascending or descending. 2 Slideshow (s) Sets how long each image stays on screen in a slideshow. From 1 to 3600 seconds; the default is 10. Videos play to the end or follow this timer, depending on the next option. 3 Play video/audio in slideshow to end Lets video and audio in a slideshow finish before moving on. Without it, the slideshow interval decides when to move to the next file. Deletion and renaming in player 4 Allow rename Allows renaming a file from inside the player. Handy while you sort: rename the current file without going back to the file browser. 5 Allow delete Allows deleting a file from inside the player. Handy while you sort: remove the current file without going back to the file browser. Undo On local resources a deleted file waits in a hidden .trash folder, so you can bring it back with Undo before the resource is closed. On some network or cloud resources a deletion is permanent. 6 Confirm delete Asks before a file is deleted in the player. Turn it off if you prefer deleting with one tap. Player interface and commands 7 Hide OS UI in fullscreen Hides the status bar and navigation in fullscreen. The picture gets the whole screen. 8 Rotate player screen with OS auto-rotate Lets the player follow the system auto-rotate. It works independently of the app-wide setting, so the rest of the app can stay as it is. 9 Show command panel by default Opens the command panel automatically when the player starts. The panel gives quick access to copy, move, delete and other file actions. 10 Player panel auto-hide duration (s) Sets how many seconds the player panel stays before it hides. A shorter time clears the screen sooner; a longer one keeps the buttons within reach. 11 Show "Black Screen" button Adds a button that blanks the screen while playback continues. It sits in the player toolbar, so the screen goes dark while audio or video keeps playing. 12 Enable Picture-in-Picture Adds a Picture-in-Picture button to the player. The player also enters Picture-in-Picture on its own when you press Home (Android 12 and newer). 13 Big Buttons Mode Makes player buttons larger and full-width. It suits car head units. The top toolbar shows 5 to 9 buttons depending on the width, and the rest move to the three-dots menu. In landscape, the tall bottom panel can reduce the playback area. 14 Compact player buttons Shrinks the bottom control buttons in the player. Useful on smaller screens or when you want a less intrusive interface. Touch zones and on-screen hints 15 Disable 9-zone tracking Switches the player from 9 touch zones to 3. With the 9-zone grid off, the player uses three zones: previous, zoom and next. Tap the left edge to open the command panel for file actions. 16 Show touch zones hint on first run Shows the touch zones hint the first time you open the player. The overlay explains the nine zones: back, copy, rename, previous, move, next, command panel, delete and slideshow. 17 Always show touch zones overlay Keeps a semi-transparent grid of touch zones over the media. It shows in fullscreen mode and helps while you learn which zone does what. 18 Show Hint Next Time Shows the touch zones hint again the next time you open the player. Use it to see the scheme once more. Background audio playback 19 Background Playback Keeps audio playing when the app is minimized. Music continues in the background. If notifications are blocked, a button appears here to manage that permission. 20 When leaving player or streams Chooses what happens to background audio when you leave the player or streams. Asking every time is the default. You can also always stop the audio or always keep it playing. The choice appears once background playback is on. 21 Show now-playing panel Shows a mini player bar while you browse images and other files. The bar lets you control the track that is playing and leads back to the full audio player. Reset 22 Reset Player settings Returns only this tab to its defaults. Settings on the other tabs keep their values. The app asks you to confirm first. pages.title: Help - Tourist
pages.description: A dashboard for a walk, a ride or a trip: speed, altitude, direction, coordinates, steps, weather and more, each on a tile. One tile is shown large at the top, the rest wait below, and buttons let you open a map, share where you are or call for help.
pages.body: Help index / Tourist Tourist What this is for A dashboard for a walk, a ride or a trip: speed, altitude, direction, coordinates, steps, weather and more, each on a tile. One tile is shown large at the top, the rest wait below, and buttons let you open a map, share where you are or call for help. In this order If a card at the top asks for a permission 1 , press its button 2 . Speed, altitude, coordinates and sun times need location; steps need physical activity. The large tile 3 shows one reading, speed to begin with. Tap any tile in the grid 14 to bring it up to the top; the app remembers your choice. Read the value 5 . Some tiles add a picture: the coordinates 6 , a compass rose 7 , an arrow 8 or a level bubble 9 . The line below 13 gives the context. Trip tiles keep adding up as you move. Reset 4 on the large tile, or Reset trip 17 , starts them again from zero. Map 15 shows where you are in a map app, and Share 16 sends your position to someone. SOS signal 18 opens the emergency signal. The Stopwatch tile has its own keys: Start / Stop 10 , Reset 11 and Open stopwatch 12 . The Counter tile opens the counter when you tap it. The elements Permission card 1 Permission required Appears when a permission is missing and says what stops working without it. Location is asked first: without it speed, altitude, coordinates and sun times cannot be shown. When location is granted but physical activity is not, the card asks for that instead and says steps are not counted. The card disappears once nothing is missing, and comes back if you withdraw a permission later. 2 Allow / Open settings Asks the system for the permission, or opens the app settings if the system will not ask again. The key says Allow while Android can still show the request. After you have declined it for good, the key says Open settings and takes you to the app page, where you can switch the permission on yourself. Location is requested as an exact and an approximate choice, so you may grant the approximate one; some tiles are then less precise. The large tile 3 Large tile The tile you are looking at, shown big at the top. It has an icon, a name, the reading and a line of detail. Speed is shown at first, and the app remembers the last tile you chose. Tapping the card itself does something only for two tiles: Coordinates copies them to the clipboard, and Counter opens the counter. On a tile whose sensor is missing the card says so, for example Sensor unavailable or Acquiring fix.. 4 Reset Starts the trip, or the step count, again from zero. The key is shown only on the tiles that accumulate: Speed, Steps, Trip distance, Ascent, Time on trip, Moving time and Average speed. On Steps it resets only the steps; on the others it resets the whole trip (distance, top speed, ascent, times and average speed together). There is no question first. Undo The trip, or the steps, return to zero at once and cannot be restored. 5 Reading The value of the tile in large digits, with its unit. Units follow the unit system chosen in Settings, Metric or US, and switch when you change it. While a sensor is warming up, the reading says why instead of showing a number: Acquiring fix.., Collecting readings.., Waiting for the sensor.. or No data yet - needs a GPS fix and internet. 6 Coordinates view Latitude and longitude, shown instead of a single number. It appears when the large tile is Coordinates and reads Lat and Lon with four decimals; before a fix it shows dashes. Tap the large card to copy the pair with five decimals; the copied text is shown for a moment. Share sends the same position. 7 Compass rose A dial that turns as you turn, with the heading in degrees. It appears when the large tile is Compass. The dial turns so that north stays north, the number is the heading in degrees and the word beside it the compass direction. The detail line says whether the reading is magnetic north or true north and warns when something near the phone, such as metal or electronics, disturbs the sensor. 8 Direction arrow An arrow that points the way a value is heading. It shows on Course, where it points the way you are moving (start moving to see it), on Wind, and on Pressure, where the arrow tilts up, down or sideways for rising, falling or steady air pressure. 9 Level bubble A spirit level for the phone: the bubble floats to the high side. It appears when the large tile is Level. Lay the phone flat and the bubble sits in the middle of the ring; a tilt of about 30 degrees pushes it to the edge. The detail line gives the pitch and roll in degrees. 10 Start / Stop Starts or stops the small stopwatch on this tile. The Stopwatch tile is a simple stopwatch of its own: one person, no laps. The key says Start while it is stopped and Stop while it runs. The reading counts minutes and seconds. It keeps counting when you turn the phone. 11 Reset Sets the tile's stopwatch back to zero and stops it. Use it between two measurements. Undo The time is lost at once and cannot be restored. 12 Open stopwatch Opens the full Stopwatch program. That program times up to four people with laps, music and a result you can send. The small stopwatch on this tile is separate and does not carry over. 13 Detail line A line under the reading that explains it. It differs from tile to tile: for Speed the top speed and the trip distance, for Satellites how many are used and in view, for Sun / Daylight sunrise and sunset, for Level the pitch and roll, and so on. When the value is only a guess it says Approximate and what it is waiting for. Other tiles 14 Other tiles All the other readings, in a grid of two columns; tap one to bring it to the top. The grid lists every tile except the one at the top. Tiles whose hardware your phone lacks are left out, not shown empty. Trip and movement: Speed, Altitude, Steps, Trip distance, Ascent, Slope, Time on trip, Moving time, Average speed, Cadence and Course. Position and sensors: Compass, Coordinates, Satellites, GPS accuracy, Level, Light, Magnetic field, Pressure and Barometric altitude. Sun and weather: Sun / Daylight, Weather, Dew point, Wind, Feels like, Humidity, UV index, Chance of precipitation, Cloud cover and Visibility. Watch: Heart rate and Body temperature, in editions that pair with a watch. Tools: Stopwatch and Counter. Steps and Cadence need a step counter and the physical activity permission, and Pressure and Barometric altitude need a barometer. The weather tiles need a GPS fix and an internet connection. The watch tiles show your watch's latest reading, or ask you to open Tourist on the watch. Action buttons 15 Map Shows your position in a map app. It hands your coordinates to the map app on the phone; with no map app installed it opens the map page in the browser. Without a fix yet, it opens the map app with no point, and if the phone has no map app, a short message says that the position is still being acquired. 16 Share Sends your position to someone as a message with a map link. It opens the system share sheet with your coordinates and a link to them on a map. Wait for a fix first; until then a message says the position is still being acquired. Whoever receives it learns where you are, so choose the recipient with care. 17 Reset Trip Starts the trip again from zero. It clears the trip distance, top speed, ascent, time on trip, moving time and average speed together. When the large tile is Steps, it resets the step count instead. It works from any tile and does not ask first. Undo The trip returns to zero at once and the values cannot be restored. 18 SOS signal Opens the SOS emergency signal. It takes you to the SOS screen, where you choose a siren, a flashing light or both, and start the signal. It is here because this screen is where you already are when something goes wrong outdoors. pages.title: Help - Wear Companion
pages.description: The Wear companion is this phone's control panel for your Wear OS watch. Choose which network resources the watch gets, set how the watch looks and behaves, pin channels for it, and use the watch from the phone: listen through its microphone, send the clipboard, ask for a screenshot.
headings: The window header and its content
Pin a channel for the watch window
pages.body: Help index / Wear Companion Wear Companion What this is for The Wear companion is this phone's control panel for your Wear OS watch. Choose which network resources the watch gets, set how the watch looks and behaves, pin channels for it, and use the watch from the phone: listen through its microphone, send the clipboard, ask for a screenshot. In this order Open the companion from the Wear Companion group on the Management tab of Settings, or from the programs. It works with a Wear OS watch paired to this phone and exists only in the editions that have it (Standard and noLegal). To send folders to the watch, press Resources for the watch 6 , tick the network resources in the list 18 , then press Push to Watch 5 . Choose how the watch behaves in the settings groups 13 and what its face buttons do 11 . Settings you change wait on the phone until you press Sync settings 2 ; face buttons and pinned channels reach the watch by themselves. The line under Sync settings 3 shows when the last sync was confirmed, or Never synced. To pin channels for the watch, open Watch stream pins 12 and press Add channels; the list that opens (19 to 24) has filters and a search. The group is there only while Streams is on. The cards and buttons in Watch operations act on the watch right now: Listen to the watch 10 , Send clipboard 8 , Request a watch screenshot 9 and Add or open the watch 7 . The links at the bottom 14 open pages of the website about the watch and send the watch face to your watch. The elements The window header and its content 1 Wear Companion The header of the window, with the way back, the sync button and the time of the last sync. The arrow closes the window. Sync settings and the line under it stay in the header even when a group below is folded, so the one button that sends your edits is always within reach. 2 Sync settings Sends the watch settings you edited on this phone to the watch. Settings you change in the groups below stay on the phone until you press this button. Pressing it sends them in one go and then waits for the watch to confirm that it applied them; the button is off while it works. If the watch does not answer in time, a short message says it may be off or out of range, and you can press again. The buttons of the watch face and the pinned channels do not wait for it - they reach the watch by themselves. 3 Sync status Says when the settings were last synced. It shows Last synced with the date and time of the last confirmed exchange, or Never synced before the first one. A press that did not reach the watch leaves the previous time in place, so the line never claims a sync that did not happen. 4 Companion content The scrolling area with every group of controls. The area is divided into folding groups: Watch operations (open from the start), Watch face buttons, Watch stream pins (only while Streams is on) and the watch settings groups Media types, Slideshow, Screen and Other, which all start folded. Tap a group's title to open or fold it; a folded settings group shows a one-line summary of its state. On a wide screen the rows sit in two columns. The controls inside are described under Inside the window. Inside the window 5 Push to Watch Sends the ticked network resources to the watch. A small window shows the progress and then the result: how many resources were sent, how many were removed from the watch because you unticked them, or a note that nothing is ticked yet. If the watch does not confirm, you can press Retry or Cancel. It sends the choice made in Resources for the watch; only SMB, FTP and SFTP resources can go to the watch. Undo Pushing again after changing the ticks replaces what the watch has. A resource you unticked is removed from the watch; ticking it and pushing again sends it back. 6 Resources for the watch Opens the list where you choose which network resources the watch gets. The button is shown only in editions that have the Wear companion. Your ticks are saved as you make them; nothing is sent until you press Push to Watch. 7 Add or open the watch Adds the watch as a resource of this phone, and opens it later. The first tap adds a resource named after your watch and a message confirms it; every later tap opens the watch's own files in the file browser. If something goes wrong, a general error message appears. 8 Send clipboard to the watch Sends the text on this phone's clipboard to the watch. A line under the button tells what came of it: the watch took the text, the clipboard was empty, no watch is within reach, or the watch declined. There is no button here to fetch the watch's clipboard: the watch sends its own from its Clipboard program, and the text lands on this phone's clipboard with a notification. 9 Request a watch screenshot Asks the watch to take a picture of its own screen. What arrives is the screen of the watch app, not the watch face or other apps. The picture does not appear here: it travels the ordinary watch-file route and a notification announces it. Under the button you see when the last screenshot arrived, with Open in Browse when the picture lies in a folder the app knows. 10 Listen to the watch Lets you hear what the watch's microphone hears. Start listening sends a request, and the watch asks its wearer to confirm. While it waits, a spinner and Stop listening let you withdraw the request; once confirmed, you hear the sound until you stop. Sound travels over Wi-Fi, not Bluetooth, so the watch must be on Wi-Fi. If the request is declined, expires or the watch is busy, a red line in the card says why. 11 Watch face buttons Chooses what the four buttons of the watch face do. Tap one of the four buttons - Left outer button, Left inner button, Right inner button or Right outer button - to open a list of choices, split into Watch sections (such as Resources, Streams or Programs), Watch programs (such as Calculator, Stopwatch, SOS or Voice recorder), App data (such as Now playing or Last opened resource), System (such as Battery, Date or Alarms) and No button, where you pick Empty. A pick reaches the watch by itself, with no need for Sync settings. The group starts folded. 12 Watch stream pins The channels the watch lists first - the same ones you pinned in Streams. The group appears only while Streams is on. It edits the pinned channels of the Streams screen, in the same order: what you pin or move here changes the Pinned section there, and the other way round. Folded, it shows how many channels are pinned. Open it to see them in order, each with Move up, Move down and Unpin, an Add channels button that opens the channel picker (the last group of this page) and Send to the watch now. Changes reach the watch on their own; Send to the watch now pushes the list again and a line says whether the watch has it. Undo Unpin removes the pin everywhere, in the Streams screen too. The channel itself stays in the catalog, and you can pin it again. 13 Watch settings groups What the watch itself shows, plays and how it looks. Four folded groups. Media types holds switches for Audio, Video, Images, Documents and Show streams. Slideshow has the switch and the interval. Screen sets the view of the home and files screens, the watch background and color scheme, and keeping the watch screen on. Other covers album art, animations, watch power saving and background playback. Changes stay on the phone until you press Sync settings. 14 Links at the bottom Pages to read more about the watch, and the way to get the watch face. All about the watch and How to install on a watch open pages of the project website in your browser. Get the watch face asks your watch to open the watch face page in Google Play, where you tap Install on the watch; with no watch connected, or a watch without Google Play, the page opens on this phone instead. Resources for the watch screen 15 Hint Says what can be sent to the watch. Only network resources - SMB, FTP and SFTP - can go to the watch, so only those are listed. Tick the ones you want it to have. 16 Select all Ticks every resource in the list. The choice is saved at once. The button is hidden while the list is empty. To clear a tick, tap its box again; there is no button that clears all of them. 17 Empty list message Tells you that there is nothing to send yet. It appears when you have no SMB, FTP or SFTP resources. Add one on the main screen, then come back to pick what the watch gets. 18 Resource list The network resources, each with a box to tick. Resources sit under a header with a count; tap the header to fold or unfold the group. The categories are Virtual resources, Internal resources and External resources, and since only network resources can go to the watch, you normally see External resources. Tap a row or its box to tick it. Every tick is saved at once, so you can leave the screen any way you like. Nothing is sent from here: press Push to Watch in the companion window. Undo Unticking changes only the choice. The resource stays on the phone; with the next push the watch drops it, and ticking it and pushing again sends it back. Pin a channel for the watch window 19 Media type Shows all channels, only audio or only video. Three buttons: All, Audio and Video. The choice combines with the topic, language and search below. 20 Topic Narrows the list to one topic. A drop-down that starts at All; pick a topic such as News or Jazz & Blues. Choosing a topic, a language or typing two letters is what lets a very large catalog show its channels at all. 21 Language Narrows the list to one language. A drop-down that starts at All. It works together with the topic and the search. 22 Sort Orders the channels in the picker. The same choices as on the Streams screen: By name, By topic, By language, By country or Recently added. It orders exactly the channels the filters and the search kept. 23 Type to search Finds a channel by typing. Type part of a name; the list narrows as you type and the cross at the end clears the field. With a very large catalog the picker first asks you to type two characters or pick a topic or language. 24 Channel list The channels you can pin - tap one to pin it. Tap a channel and the window closes at once: the channel is pinned at the top of the pinned list, which is also the Pinned section of Streams. At most two hundred channels are shown; if more match, a line says how many and asks you to refine the search. A tap outside the window closes it without pinning anything. pages.title: Help - Welcome wizard
pages.description: The welcome wizard runs on first launch and walks you through language, theme, device profile, network sources, capabilities, permissions and the default player. You can open it again from Settings.
headings: How will you use this device?
pages.body: Help index / Welcome wizard Welcome wizard What this is for The welcome wizard runs on first launch and walks you through language, theme, device profile, network sources, capabilities, permissions and the default player. You can open it again from Settings. In this order On the first page, choose your language 6 and theme 7 . Everything you pick in the wizard can be changed later in Settings, so there is no wrong choice here. Press Next 3 to reach the device profile page and tap the tile 8 that matches your device. It tunes the defaults for you; tapping the selected tile again moves you on. Switch on the network sources you plan to use (10, 11, 12). The page is left out when the edition has none of them. On the capabilities page, turn on what you need (15 to 23) - audio, video, documents, text recognition, translation, streams, gestures. Optional parts download right there. On the permissions page, press Grant All 25 to go through the requests one by one. A permission you skip stays off, and you can come back to it later. If your edition offers it, make FastMediaSorter the default app for audio, video, images and documents (28 to 31). Press Finish 4 to close the wizard. Previous 1 steps back, Enable all 2 on the first page does the whole setup in one go, and Help 5 opens this page. The elements Navigation 1 Previous Goes back one page. It is hidden on the first page, where there is nothing to go back to. 2 Enable all Does the whole setup in one go. It is on the first page only. First it explains what will happen, then lets you confirm your device profile, and only after that turns everything on, asks for the permissions and the default-app choice, and finishes. The pages in between are skipped. Undo Nothing is applied until you confirm the device profile; Back or a tap outside applies nothing. Anything it turned on can be changed later in Settings. 3 Next Moves to the next page. On the last page it is replaced by Finish. 4 Finish Saves your device profile and closes the wizard. Permissions are granted on their own page, so Finish asks for nothing more. It appears on the last page in place of Next. 5 Help Opens help for this screen. You get the usual order of the wizard and what each control does. Welcome 6 Select app language Opens the list of app languages. The wizard reloads in the language you pick. You can change the language later in Settings. 7 Select app theme Picks Auto, Light or Dark for the whole app. Auto follows your device. The theme is applied immediately, so you see the result at once. How will you use this device? 8 Device profile Picks the kind of device you are setting up. Tiles cover a personal smartphone, tablet, TV box, car head unit, photo frame, e-book reader and more, and the one that fits best is marked as recommended. A profile tunes many defaults at once. Other keeps the settings as they are. Undo You can change the profile later in Settings. 9 Primary window Chooses what the app opens as: device home screen, in-app desktop or main screen. This choice appears only in editions that include the home surface. The recommended option is marked. Network resources 10 Local network (Ethernet) SMB Turns on shared folders on your local network. For example a shared folder on a Windows PC, a NAS such as Synology or QNAP, or a USB disk plugged into your router. 11 Computer on the internet (S)FTP Turns on servers reached over FTP and SFTP. For example a hosting account over FTP, your own home server over SFTP, or a camera that uploads photos to an FTP folder. 12 In cloud resources Turns on cloud storage: Google Drive, OneDrive and Dropbox. For example, sign in to Google Drive once and browse your photo backup like any other folder. The row is hidden in editions without cloud support. 13 Get the Windows app Opens the page for the Windows companion app. If your media sits on a Windows PC, the companion shares those folders to this device in a couple of clicks, with no server setup. 14 Media exchange between devices Opens the guide to exchanging media between devices. Read it when you want to move files between your own devices. What should the app do? 15 Allow All Files mode Allows the All Files mode. This switch only permits the mode, so you still turn it on for each resource. 16 Audio Turns on music and audio. Play music and audio, and sort tracks into folders. 17 Video Turns on video. Play videos and sort clips with the built-in player. 18 Documents Turns on documents. Open PDF, text, e-books and office files. 19 Text recognition (OCR) Turns on text recognition for images and scans. Recognize text and copy it. The recognition pack downloads right on this page, with progress shown under the row, and the feature turns on once the download has succeeded. 20 Translation Turns on translation of recognized and selected text. Works offline. The translation pack downloads right on this page, and the feature turns on once the download has succeeded. 21 Streams Turns on internet streams. Play internet streams and import the built-in catalog. The catalog is imported right on this page, with progress shown under the row. 22 Statistics collection Turns on usage statistics. They are collected on your device and nothing is sent automatically. 23 Enable gestures Turns on swipes from the left edge of the screen. The swipes open the menu and take a screenshot, normal or silent. Android may ask for the Display over other apps permission first. 24 All downloadable (optional) elements Opens the list of downloadable, optional parts of the app. Install the ones you want now, or leave them for later: you can also reach the same list from Settings. Permissions 25 Grant All Walks you through all the permission requests. First comes one Android dialog for the regular permissions, then the special ones open as separate system screens, one at a time. Turn the switch on there and press Back to continue. 26 Open App Settings Opens the Android settings page of this app. Use it when you want to review or change a permission yourself, or when Android no longer shows its own request. 27 "A few" permissions Lists every permission this edition can ask for. Each row says what the permission is for and has its own button to grant it or open the matching settings. Opting out means leaving a permission off; nothing is hidden from you. Default Player 28 Audio Makes FastMediaSorter the app that plays your audio files. Android shows its own dialog: pick FastMediaSorter and tap Always. This is not permanent - Android keeps the choice in its own settings, and you can change it back there. 29 Video Makes FastMediaSorter the app that plays your videos. Android shows its own dialog: pick FastMediaSorter and tap Always. This is not permanent - Android keeps the choice in its own settings, and you can change it back there. 30 Images Makes FastMediaSorter the app that opens your images. Android shows its own dialog: pick FastMediaSorter and tap Always. This is not permanent - Android keeps the choice in its own settings, and you can change it back there. 31 Documents Makes FastMediaSorter the app that opens your documents. Android shows its own dialog: pick FastMediaSorter and tap Always. This is not permanent - Android keeps the choice in its own settings, and you can change it back there. pages.title: Editing Photos - Rotate, Crop, Colors and GIF Tools
pages.description: How to turn or mirror a photo for good, crop it, save a smaller copy, change brightness, contrast and saturation, apply black-and-white, sepia or negative filters, and change the speed of an animated GIF or cut it into frames.
headings: Turn or mirror a photo for good
Crop away what you do not want
Save a smaller copy to send
Fix brightness and colors, or add a filter
Change the speed of a GIF, keep its first frame, or cut it into frames
Edit in a separate window on a large screen
Viewing photos, GIFs and zoom gestures
pages.body: Images, Audio & Slideshow All editions Recipe #02 Editing Photos - Rotate, Crop, Colors and GIF Tools Turn, mirror and crop a photo, make a small copy to send, brighten a dark picture or give it a black-and-white look, and change the speed of an animated GIF - right in the image viewer , without a separate editor. Why You'll Love This A photo of a receipt came out sideways, a holiday picture has a stranger at the edge, an old scan is too dark, or you want a tiny copy of a big photo to send by message. You do not need a separate photo editor for these everyday fixes: the image viewer has them built in, one tap away from the picture you are looking at. The same place also holds a few tools for animated GIF, WebP and APNG pictures: make an animation faster or slower, keep its first frame as a normal picture, or take it apart frame by frame. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter in any edition : Standard, noLegal, Lite, Photos, Legacy, VR or FOSS. A picture you are allowed to change. Pictures in a folder the app can only read are saved as a new file in your Downloads folder instead. Pictures in a network folder can be edited too, in the editions that can open network folders (all except Lite). For cutting animated WebP or APNG pictures into frames: Android 9 or newer. GIF files work on any Android version. These changes are saved to the file straight away Every button in the Image Edit window changes the original picture at once - there is no separate Save step and no confirmation. If you want to keep the original, copy the file first (see Copy, move and delete files ) or use Crop to file and Compressed copy , which always make a new file. 1 Open the editing tools Open the photo in the image viewer. Then either tap the pencil button Adjust on the command panel , or open the three-dots menu and tap Adjust . For an ordinary photo this opens the Image Edit window with four groups: Rotation , Flip , Filters and Adjustments . For an animated GIF, WebP or APNG picture it opens the GIF Editor instead (see step 6). The Image Edit window. 2 Turn or mirror a photo for good In the Rotation group tap ↺ 90° to turn the photo a quarter to the left, ↻ 90° to turn it a quarter to the right, or 180° to turn it upside down. In the Flip group tap Flip ↔ to mirror it left to right or Flip ↕ to mirror it top to bottom. The photo is rewritten on the spot while "Rotating image.." is shown. Its date, camera details and other information stored inside the file are kept, and the turn is stored in the picture itself, so it looks right in every other app too. 3 Crop away what you do not want Open the three-dots menu and choose one of two commands: Crop - cuts the photo and replaces the original file. Crop to file - keeps the original and saves the cut part as a new file. A frame with handles appears over the photo. Drag the corners and edges until the frame holds only the part you want to keep, then confirm with OK . For Crop to file you are asked for a file name; the suggested one is the original name plus _crop- and the date and time, for example beach_crop-260924-1530.jpg . The new file goes into the same folder, or into Downloads when the folder cannot be written to. Drag the handles, then tap OK. 4 Save a smaller copy to send Open the three-dots menu and tap Compressed copy . The app saves a lighter JPEG copy of the photo next to the original (or in Downloads, if that folder is read-only), named like beach_compress-260924-1530.jpg . The original is not touched. A compressed copy is handy when a messenger or an e-mail refuses a large photo. The copy looks the same on a phone screen but takes much less space. 5 Fix brightness and colors, or add a filter In the Adjustments group move the sliders: Brightness - from -100 (much darker) to +100 (much lighter); 0 leaves it as it is. Contrast - from 0x (flat and gray) to 2x (strong); 1x leaves it as it is. Saturation - from 0x (black and white) to 2x (vivid colors); 1x leaves it as it is. Tap Apply Adjustments to save the result into the photo. The Filters group changes the whole picture with one tap: Grayscale makes it black and white, Sepia gives it the warm brown look of an old print, and Negative swaps every color for its opposite. Brightness, Contrast and Saturation sliders. Pictures on another computer When the photo is in a network folder , for example a shared folder on your home computer (see Windows network shares ), the app downloads it, makes the change and uploads it back to the same place. It takes a little longer, but you do not have to copy anything by hand. 6 Change the speed of a GIF, keep its first frame, or cut it into frames Open an animated picture and tap Adjust . The GIF Editor window offers three tools: Animation Speed - move the slider between 0.25x (four times slower) and 4x (four times faster), then tap Apply Speed Change . For a GIF on this device the original file is rewritten with the new speed; for a GIF in a network folder a new file such as party_speed_2_0x.gif is saved to Downloads. Save First Frame as Image - saves the first picture of the animation as a still PNG in Downloads, named like party_first_frame.png . Extract All Frames - saves every frame as a separate PNG picture: party_frame_001.png , party_frame_002.png and so on. For a file on this device they go into the same folder; for a file in a network folder, into Downloads. The GIF Editor window. 7 Edit in a separate window on a large screen On a Chromebook, a tablet or a headset the player can open a picture in its own window beside other apps: open the three-dots menu and tap Open in new window . If you do not see this item, turn on Allow new windows in Settings , the General tab, Interface (see multi-window and foldables ). In the separate window the three-dots menu groups every editing command under one Editing section: Adjust , Crop , Crop to file , Compressed copy , Drawing , Rotate 90° and Rotate -90° . The same menu also lets you rename the file and switch Screen autorotate on or off. What You Get Sideways photos stand upright in every app, unwanted edges are gone, dark pictures are brighter, and you have small copies ready to send. Animated pictures play at the speed you like, and any frame of them can become an ordinary picture. Tips and Troubleshooting Keep the original. Crop, rotate, flip, filters and adjustments overwrite the file. Only Crop to file , Compressed copy , Save First Frame as Image and Extract All Frames always create new files. Just want to look at a sideways photo? Use Rotate 90° in the three-dots menu of the viewer. It turns the picture on screen only and leaves the file alone - see Viewing photos, GIFs and zoom gestures . Want to draw or write on a photo? That is a separate tool - see drawing and image markup . A new file landed in Downloads? That happens when the photo's folder cannot be written to, for example a folder the app may only read. Move the file where you want it afterwards. What to Try Next: Related Recipes Photos Viewing photos, GIFs and zoom gestures Swipe through photos, zoom into details and pause animations. pages.body: Images, Audio & Slideshow All editions Recipe #03 Creating Photo Slideshows A slideshow moves from one photo to the next by itself. Choose how long each photo stays, add background music, and let the app keep the screen on - a phone or tablet becomes a photo frame in a minute. Why You'll Love This Relatives are visiting and you want to show the holiday photos on the TV without swiping every few seconds. Or an old tablet on the shelf could become a photo frame that shows a new family picture every minute. A slideshow does exactly that: it moves to the next photo by itself, after the number of seconds you choose, and can play music in the background. A slideshow is only a way of looking. It never creates a video and never changes your files. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter in any edition . In the Photos edition the slideshow shows pictures only, because that edition does not play video or audio. A resource with photos, for example a folder on this device or a network folder on your home computer. Optional: a second resource with music, if you want background music. 1 Start the slideshow Open the first photo of the folder in the image viewer and tap Slideshow on the control bar. The button turns red while the slideshow runs. Tap it again to stop. There is also a shortcut on the main screen : some resources show a small Start slideshow icon on their card, which opens the folder and starts the slideshow in one tap. The slideshow walks through the folder in the same order as the file browser . The next photo replaces the previous one at once, without fades or other effects. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Slideshow running Player showing a photo, control bar visible, Slideshow button active (red). Profile: phone ID: images.slideshow-button-active The screen stays on by itself While the slideshow runs, the screen does not go dark - you will see the message "Screen will stay on during slideshow". When you stop it, your usual screen timeout comes back. 2 Choose how long each photo stays Each photo stays on screen for 10 seconds unless you choose otherwise. You can set a different time for every resource: on the main screen open the resource for editing, expand Advanced Settings and type the number of seconds into Slideshow Interval (seconds) . Anything from 1 second to 3600 seconds (one hour) works. Tap Save Changes . The default for new resources is in Settings , the Player tab, section Sorting, slideshow and playback order , field Slideshow (s) . The Slideshow Interval field in the resource editor. 3 Watch the countdown A few seconds before the next photo appears, a small countdown - 3, 2, 1 - shows in the corner. It tells you the photo is about to change, so you can stop the slideshow in time if you want to look longer. The countdown appears whenever a photo stays longer than three seconds. The countdown before the next photo. 4 Change the slideshow on the fly Press and hold the Slideshow button. The Slideshow Settings window opens: Default slideshow (sec.) - a slider from 1 to 60 seconds for the current session. Play videos/audio to end - when this is on, a video or a song in the folder plays to its end before the slideshow moves on, and no countdown is shown for it. Background Music - tap to pick one music file from your phone to play during this slideshow; the name of the chosen track is shown below, and a clear button removes it. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Slideshow Settings window Slideshow Settings dialog over a photo, interval at 5 s, play-to-end on. Profile: phone ID: images.slideshow-settings-dialog 5 Play music from a whole music folder For a slideshow with music every time, go to Settings , the Media tab, section Images, GIFs and slideshow , turn on Play music during slideshow , tap Select Music Source and choose the resource that holds your music. From now on every slideshow of photos and GIFs plays the tracks of that resource in random order. You can mix places freely: photos from a network folder and music from this device, or the other way round. Play music during slideshow in Settings. 6 Show photos while music plays It also works the other way round: listen to music and let photos change in the background. Go to Settings , the Media tab, section Audio playback, covers and visuals , turn on Show random photos during audio playback and pick the resource with your photos. Now open a song in the audio player and tap Slideshow . The music controls step aside and a full-screen photo appears, replaced by another random photo at every slideshow interval. More about backgrounds for music is in Playing and organizing music files . What You Get Your photos change by themselves at the pace you chose, with a short countdown before each change, music in the background if you want it, and videos and songs that play to the end. The screen stays on for as long as the show runs. Tips and Troubleshooting The slideshow stopped with "Connection to .. was lost"? The network folder became unreachable, for example the computer went to sleep or Wi-Fi dropped. Start the slideshow again when the connection is back. The slideshow stopped with "No access to .."? Three files in a row could not be opened. Check that the folder is still there and that the app may still read it. Videos interrupt your photo show? Turn off Play videos/audio to end , or limit the resource to pictures in its settings. Photos are cut at the edges? Turn off Crop images to fill screen in Settings, Media, Images, GIFs and slideshow - see Viewing photos, GIFs and zoom gestures . The slideshow does not start for a music or video library? Resources set up with the Audio Library or Video Library resource profile play their files one after another on their own and do not use the slideshow timer. pages.body: Images, Audio & Slideshow All editions Recipe #01 Viewing Photos, GIFs and Zoom Gestures The image viewer shows one picture at a time on the whole screen. Swipe to move between photos, pinch to zoom, turn a sideways photo for a moment and pause animated pictures - all without changing your files. Why You'll Love This You come back from a trip with four hundred photos and want to look through them quickly, one after another, on the whole screen. Or a friend sends you a funny animated GIF and you want to stop it on the best frame. The image viewer is made for exactly this: one picture at a time, a swipe to the next one, and nothing in the way. Nothing on this page changes your files. Zooming, turning a photo for a moment and pausing an animation only change what you see right now. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter installed. The image viewer is part of every edition : Standard, noLegal, Lite, Photos, Legacy, VR and FOSS. At least one resource with pictures in it, for example the All Images collection or a folder you added yourself. For HEIC and HEIF photos (the format many phones use for camera shots): Android 9 or newer. For AVIF pictures: Android 12 or newer. 1 Open a photo full screen Open a resource on the main screen , then tap any picture in the file browser . The picture opens in the image viewer , filling the screen. The viewer shows JPG, PNG, WebP, BMP and GIF pictures, animated WebP and APNG, and HEIC, HEIF and AVIF photos. If your Android is too old for HEIC or AVIF, the viewer does not fail silently: it tells you which Android version the picture needs, for example "requires Android 9 (API 28) or newer". A photo opened full screen in the image viewer. 2 Move to the next or previous photo Swipe from right to left to see the next picture in the folder, and from left to right to go back to the previous one. The order is the same as in the file browser, so if you sorted the folder by date, you walk through your photos by date. You can also tap the screen instead of swiping. The screen is divided into invisible touch zones : a tap on the right side of the middle row opens the next file, a tap on the left side opens the previous one. Keyboard and remote control On a tablet with a keyboard, or on a TV box with a remote, the left and right arrow keys move between photos too. See keyboard, D-pad and TV navigation . 3 Zoom in to see the details Put two fingers on the picture and spread them apart to zoom in; pinch them together to zoom out. While zoomed in, drag with one finger to look around the picture. By default the viewer loads a lighter copy of each picture, about 1920 pixels wide, so large photos open quickly. To see every pixel of a 50-megapixel photo when you zoom in - and to zoom while the command panel is open - go to Settings , the Media tab, the Images, GIFs and slideshow section, and turn on Load images at full resolution . Pinch to zoom in on a photo. 4 Turn a sideways photo for a moment Some photos are shown lying on their side. To look at one upright without changing the file, open the three-dots menu and tap Rotate 90° (turn clockwise) or Rotate -90° (turn counter-clockwise). Each tap turns the picture by a quarter; four taps bring it back. This turn lasts only while you look at the photo. The file itself stays exactly as it was, and the phone's own screen rotation is not touched. To turn the photo for good, use the editing tools described in Editing photos: rotate, crop, colors and GIF tools . Rotate 90° and Rotate -90° in the three-dots menu. 5 Play and pause animated GIF, WebP and APNG pictures Animated pictures start moving as soon as you open them, just like in a messaging app. This works for GIF files and also for animated WebP and APNG pictures. To stop on a frame, tap the play and pause button on the control bar. Tap it again and the animation continues from where it stopped. When you move to another file and come back, the viewer remembers whether you left this animation playing or paused. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Paused GIF A GIF open in the player, paused, control bar visible with the play button. Profile: phone ID: images.viewer-gif-paused More you can do with an animation Speed an animation up or slow it down, save its first frame as a picture, or cut it into separate frames - all of this is in Editing photos: rotate, crop, colors and GIF tools . 6 Choose between the whole picture and a full screen A photo rarely has exactly the shape of your screen. By default the viewer shows the whole picture and leaves thin empty bars at the edges, so nothing is cut off. If you prefer the picture to cover the entire screen, go to Settings , the Media tab, the Images, GIFs and slideshow section, and turn on Crop images to fill screen . The edges of the picture that do not fit are then hidden. The same choice applies to the slideshow . The Crop images to fill screen switch in Settings, Media, Images, GIFs and slideshow. What You Get You can walk through a whole folder of photos with a swipe, zoom into any detail, straighten a sideways shot for a moment and freeze an animation on the frame you like - without changing a single file. Tips and Troubleshooting Zoom looks blurry? Turn on Load images at full resolution in Settings, Media, Images, GIFs and slideshow. The viewer then loads the original picture instead of a lighter copy. A HEIC or AVIF photo shows a notice instead of a picture? Your Android version cannot draw that format. The notice names the Android version the picture needs. You can still copy, move and share the file. Sort while you look. The same full-screen player can copy, move or delete the photo you are looking at. See Copy, move and delete files . Let the photos change by themselves. Start a slideshow and the viewer moves to the next picture on its own. pages.body: Launcher: Gadgets and Widgets Standard and noLegal Recipe #02 Placing, Resizing and Styling Gadgets and Widgets on the Launcher Desktop A gadget needs a good place and the right size. This page shows how to put gadgets and the app's widgets on the launcher desktop , let the desktop make room, resize them, choose how solid their card is, and start again with a fresh set. Why You'll Love This A gadget is only useful where your eye falls: the clock big and on top, the weather beside it, the battery small in a corner. This page is about the placing - where a gadget goes, how big it is, and how much of the wallpaper shows behind it. The same steps work for the app's own widgets , which can live on the launcher desktop as well as on the Android home screen . Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter in the Standard edition or the noLegal edition , with the launcher desktop switched on - see Your launcher desktop . For the app's widgets on the desktop: FastMediaSorter set as the device home screen. 1 Put a gadget on the desktop Touch and hold an empty square, tap Add an item.. , choose Gadget and pick one. It lands where you pressed, at its starting size. What each gadget does is described in Desktop gadgets . No empty square in sight? Tap Edit the desktop in the long-press menu, then the + button next to Done on the taskbar : the new item goes into the first free place, or into a new row below everything. 2 Let the desktop make room A gadget often needs more than one square. When you add it to a spot that is too small, the squares below slide down to make room - nothing is covered and nothing is lost. If there is truly no way to fit it, you are told so instead of nothing happening: No room on the launcher desktop. Free a spot and try again. Remove or move something, or add another screen - see Arranging the desktop . 3 Bring one of the app's widgets to the desktop The app's widgets - calculator, camera, photo frame, music, recorder, favorites, scheduled operations and others - can sit on the launcher desktop too. Open Settings , the Management tab, and tap Add a gadget to the launcher desktop ; the chosen one goes into the first free place and a short message says Added to the launcher desktop . The button is shown only while the launcher is on. Some widgets need to be set up first. Random Photo Frame asks which resource to take photos from, and Quick capture asks which folder to save to. The square is placed only after you confirm; if you cancel, nothing is placed and nothing is left behind. A widget on the desktop and the same widget on another home screen keep their own settings - two photo frames can show two different albums. Removing a square also forgets its settings. All widgets are described in FastMediaSorter widgets for your home screen . Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Adding a widget to the desktop Settings, Management tab, scrolled to the two widget buttons, launcher on, portrait. Profile: phone ID: launcher.widgets-add-from-settings 4 Make a gadget bigger or smaller Tap Edit the desktop in the long-press menu. Every square now shows a card, and each gadget has a handle in its corner. Drag the handle to make the gadget bigger or smaller - from its starting size up to the whole screen. Tap Done when it looks right. The size is remembered, also after a restart. A few gadgets keep a sensible minimum: Clock goes down to two squares by one, and Translator always stays at least two rows high so its text and result fit. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Resizing a gadget Desktop in edit mode, a Weather gadget mid-resize, portrait. Profile: phone ID: launcher.widgets-resize-handle 5 Choose how solid the gadget card is Behind each gadget there is a light card. To make it lighter or heavier, open the launcher settings - from the long-press menu, from the Start menu, or through Settings , General , System launcher settings - and in the Appearance group tap Widget backdrop opacity . Pick from 0% (Transparent) , which lets the wallpaper show through, to 100% (Opaque) ; 25% (Default) is the starting value. The choice stays after a restart. While you arrange the desktop every square shows the full card anyway, so its edges are easy to see. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Widget backdrop opacity Launcher settings, Appearance group, the opacity list open, portrait. Profile: phone ID: launcher.widgets-backdrop-opacity 6 Start again with a fresh set of gadgets In the System group of the launcher settings, Reset launcher settings returns the desktop to its first state after a confirmation. It asks how densely to lay the icons out ( Grid density : Sparse , Standard , Dense or Very dense ) and opens on the choice that suits your device profile . The starter Gadgets section is filled for your kind of device too: a photo frame gets an Image window , an e-book reader a Document window , a VR headset a Battery square. The settings of widgets you had placed are cleared with the reset, so nothing is left behind. What You Get Every gadget and widget sits where you want it, at the size you chose, with as much or as little card behind it as you like - and it stays that way after a restart. Tips and Troubleshooting A gadget could not start? The rest of the desktop stays usable, and a message names the square: for example Map could not start. The rest of your desktop is available. Remove that square and add it again, or leave it for now. Want the layout to stay put? Lock the desktop so a stray touch cannot move a gadget - see Arranging the desktop . A gadget swallows your swipes? Gadgets keep their own gestures: a map still pans and a list still scrolls. Start the swipe on an empty spot instead. pages.title: Help - Water flashlight
pages.description: The water flashlight lights the camera flash and the whole screen at full brightness together, then locks the screen against touch. It is made for wet hands - rain, a shower - where a touch screen presses itself. You leave it with a volume button, never by touching the glass.
pages.body: Help index / Water flashlight Water flashlight What this is for The water flashlight lights the camera flash and the whole screen at full brightness together, then locks the screen against touch. It is made for wet hands - rain, a shower - where a touch screen presses itself. You leave it with a volume button, never by touching the glass. In this order Open Water flashlight from the programs menu, the programs panel or a home-screen widget. If it is not offered, switch it on first in Settings, on the Management tab, in the group Additional programs and scenarios. The camera flash and the screen 1 light up together at once. From this moment the screen is locked. Only the time 2 and the reminder 3 are shown, and touching the glass does nothing: wet fingers or drops cannot close, dim or press anything. The hint Locked. Use the buttons 3 means the volume buttons 4 . To switch the light off, press a volume button 4 : volume up, volume down or mute. The screen closes when you let go of the key, and the volume does not change. The screen stays awake for as long as the light is on, so you do not need to touch the phone to keep it lit. If you leave another way 5 - the power button or a system gesture - the flash goes out as well, so it never keeps burning in a pocket. Do not rely on a gesture in water: drops can trigger it and the light disappears. The elements The lit screen 1 Lit screen A white screen at full brightness with the camera flash on, deaf to every touch. The window is white at the highest brightness and the camera flash burns together with it. A phone without a camera flash still works: the lit screen is then the only light. Only the brightness of this window is raised, never the brightness setting of the phone, so after you leave it the phone is as bright as before. Every touch on the screen is swallowed on purpose, so water on the glass cannot close or change anything. The status bar and the navigation buttons are hidden for the same reason. A deliberate swipe from the screen edge can still bring the system bars back for a moment. Time and reminder 2 Clock The time in large black digits, readable at arm's length. It moves on at the start of every minute. Whether it reads in 12 or 24 hours follows the unit system of the app (Metric shows 24 hours, US shows 12), not the clock format of the device. It is only a display and cannot be touched. 3 Locked. Use the buttons Reminds you that touch is off and that a button is the way out. The line is always on the screen, so you do not have to remember how to leave in the dark or in the rain. The buttons it speaks of are the hardware buttons of the phone, first of all the volume buttons. Tapping the text does nothing. How to leave 4 Volume buttons The way out: press a volume button and the light goes out. Volume up, volume down and mute close the screen and put out the flash. The screen closes when you release the key, and that press is swallowed, so the volume of your music or calls does not change. The camera key, the button on a headset and the play/pause media key do the same on devices that have them. The Back button is deliberately not one of the exit keys: with gesture navigation Back arrives from a swipe across the glass, and wet glass makes such swipes by itself. A device with no volume buttons has to use the other ways out below. Shortcut Volume up / Volume down / Mute 5 Power button and system gestures Other ways out. They also put the light out, but water can trigger them. The screen does not pin itself and does not block system gestures. The power button turns the display off, and a Home or app-switch gesture takes you to another screen; in both cases the flash goes out at once, so it cannot be left burning in a pocket or a bag. In water do not count on these: a drop on the glass can cause a gesture, and then the light disappears when you need it. Use a volume button when you want to switch it off yourself. pages.body: Launcher: Taskbar, Menus and Gestures Standard and noLegal Recipe #08 Desktop Context Menus and Fast Actions - What a Long Press Opens A long press on the launcher desktop is rarely just one thing. This page walks through what each long press opens - on a resource, a channel, an app function - and through the squares that build or update themselves on their own: new resources, app shortcuts, contacts, a shared place, live channel windows and a few small helpers. Why You'll Love This A long press on the FastMediaSorter desktop rarely does just one thing. Depending on what you're holding, it can open a rich menu, start creating something new, or turn a shared contact, place or channel into a square that keeps itself current from then on. This page is a tour of what each long press offers, and of the squares that build or update themselves on their own - so nothing on the desktop ever feels like a mystery. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter in the Standard edition or the noLegal edition , with the launcher desktop open - see Your launcher desktop . A few empty squares to try the menus and the new squares on. Optional: a contact, a channel, or a place shared from a map app, if you want to try those specific squares. 1 Long-press menus on cells Touch and hold any square on the desktop and a menu opens that matches what you're holding. A resource or channel square opens the same menu the main app offers for that item: for a resource, open it, play it, add another shortcut , edit it, copy it, export it, share access to it, rescan it or delete it; for a channel, pin it, add a shortcut, share its link, or remove it. Both menus come from one shared list the app keeps for each kind of item, so the desktop and the main window never drift apart, and the same confirmation guards a destructive action either way. An App functions square - Streams, Quick Camera, Network Monitor and the rest - opens a shorter menu: Open , Settings where the feature has one, Pin to taskbar , and Remove from desktop . Some squares reach further than opening themselves. A square pinned to a quick-access panel route opens that panel directly, and a square pinned to a scheduled operation asks you to confirm, then runs the job in the background - a backup you can start with one long press instead of digging through settings. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Cell action menu Launcher desktop, long press on a resource square, the full action menu open, portrait. Profile: phone ID: launcher.cell-action-menu 2 Resources straight from home Starting a brand-new resource - a folder, a cloud account, a network share - no longer means leaving the desktop first. Touch and hold an empty square and tap Add resource , or, while adding My resource from the ordinary add-item picker, tap Add resource.. at the bottom of the list. Either opens the app's usual resource-creation screen; finish it and the new resource's shortcut lands on the desktop by itself. Cancelling leaves nothing behind, and on a home screen that won't accept a pinned shortcut the resource is still created - the app just says so. Every resource you create this way, or from the main window, lands in the desktop's Resources section automatically, and that section keeps its own Add resource square at the end, so you're never short of an empty one to start the next. A resource's square shows its real face on the desktop and the taskbar : the icon you picked for it, or its virtual-folder or cloud-provider glyph, layered with a small badge for how it connects - cloud, network or local - instead of one generic icon per resource type. Turn on a media type later, say All Images , and its own aggregate square appears in Resources by itself, without touching anything else you've arranged. The App functions squares keep themselves current too: switching a feature on adds its square there at once, in both the upright and sideways layout, and switching it off removes that square again - one you removed by hand stays gone either way. Installing a real app adds one automatic square of its own to the desktop; uninstalling it removes only that automatic square, never one you placed yourself. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Resources section Launcher desktop, Resources section, two resource squares with composed logos and the Add resource square, portrait. Profile: phone ID: launcher.resources-section-auto-add 3 Squares for people Share a contact with the launcher and it becomes a square that keeps working for that person, without asking for your address book up front. Pin a contact from the add-item picker and choose what the square does: open their Contact card , Call them, Send SMS , or open Message in an app to jump straight into a messenger conversation. Call and SMS are hidden on a device with no telephony. The app reads the contact once, from the entry you pick in the system contact picker, and keeps a snapshot on the square - no contacts permission is needed just to pin one, and calling always goes through the number you actually chose. Until a photo is on file, or if you never grant the permission below, the square shows the person's initials over a color that stays theirs. Pinning a messenger square first asks Which app should open the chat? so you pick the app before the person; an Any app row keeps the older order of person-then-app, and the question is skipped when only one messenger is installed. If the person turns out to have no chat in the app you picked, the square's error message says which app that was. Want the square to stay current when someone changes their photo or gets renamed? Grant the contacts permission when the app asks, right as you pin the square. Refuse and the square keeps working from the snapshot taken at pin time, which also stands in if the contact is later deleted or can't be read. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Contact square Launcher desktop, a pinned contact square with a live photo next to one showing initials on a color block, portrait. Profile: phone ID: launcher.contact-cell-live-photo 4 A place from the map Share a location from any map app while the launcher is turned on, and Add place to launcher appears in the share sheet next to your other sharing choices. Tap it, and a square lands on the desktop that opens turn-by-turn navigation to that spot, ready to start driving the moment you tap it. A shared short link is resolved to real coordinates while the square is created, so opening it later needs no network. When a link can't be resolved, the square is still created and simply shows the place as shared. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Add place to launcher Share sheet opened from a maps app, the Add place to launcher target visible, portrait. Profile: phone ID: launcher.place-shortcut-share-sheet 5 Live windows onto radio, video and maps A channel can sit on the desktop as more than a shortcut. Choose Stream in the add-item picker, or long-press a channel square and choose Add window to desktop , and you get a Stream window : a radio channel shows its name, icon and a play/pause button; a video channel gets a larger square, at least 3x2, with the picture itself paused on the last frame until you press play - nothing starts on its own. Tap a playing video window and corner controls fade in for a moment: play/pause, mute, stop, fullscreen and picture-in-picture. Fullscreen and picture-in-picture both hand off to the full player, which can collapse back into a small floating window on request. Adding a channel square before you've saved any channels opens Settings , Streams instead of an empty list, so there's always somewhere to go. Picking a channel for any of these squares stays quick even with a very long list: only the icons on screen get loaded, a big catalog asks for a search word or a topic first, and an empty result says so instead of leaving a spinner on screen. The same fast picker also serves the channel choosers of the Legacy and VR editions , which use it outside the launcher desktop. YouTube channel window works the same idea for a channel you follow there: name it or paste its address, and its square - at least 3x2 - shows the channel name and the cover of its latest upload, silent until you tap it, then plays that video right inside the square through YouTube's own player. Where the device can't host that player, the square opens the channel in the YouTube app instead. Google Maps Live Frame puts an interactive map, not a screenshot, on the desktop: pan and zoom it like the map app itself, right from the square. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Stream window controls Launcher desktop, a 3x2 video Stream window square, overlay controls visible after a tap, portrait. Profile: phone ID: launcher.stream-window-overlay-controls 6 Helpers: translation, playback and weather A few squares do small jobs well, right where you are. The Translator square translates typed or pasted text fully offline, through the bundled engine; its caption shows the language pair and doubles as a button to change it. It says plainly when a language pack is still missing rather than failing quietly. The Now Playing gadget starts out showing this app's own playback, the same as ever. Turn on notification access from a button on the gadget itself - behind a plain-language explanation of what that grants - and it follows and controls whatever is playing in any app instead, falling back to FastMediaSorter's own playback whenever nothing else is. It draws the cover art the playing app publishes, falls back to that app's icon when there is none, and a tap on the card opens whichever app is currently playing. The weather square's Unit system - metric or US measurements - lives in Settings , General , and without you touching it the square already shows Fahrenheit on a device set to the United States, Liberia or Myanmar, and Celsius everywhere else, read from the device's region rather than its language. The city you picked for it is remembered on its own, so resetting the launcher to defaults brings the weather back already showing your city instead of asking again. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Now Playing artwork Launcher desktop, Now Playing gadget showing an external app's cover art and controls, portrait. Profile: phone ID: launcher.now-playing-artwork What You Get Every square on your desktop opens the right menu for what it holds, new resources and app squares add themselves as you create or install things, and people, places, channels and a handful of small helpers all turn into squares that stay live and current - without you hunting through settings first. Tips and Troubleshooting Interrupted while picking something for a new square? If Android needs to close the app in the background while you're still in a picker - choosing a contact, an app or a resource - the square you started keeps its place. Finish the picker when you come back and it drops in exactly where you began. Using a keyboard or a TV remote? See Keyboard, D-pad and Android TV control for how to reach these same menus without a long press.
