pages.title: Help - Settings: Management
pages.description: Management is where you set how files are copied, moved and deleted, which resources are Quick Sort destinations, what the app records and runs in the background, and which extra programs and gestures are on.
pages.body: Help index / Settings: Management Settings: Management What this is for Management is where you set how files are copied, moved and deleted, which resources are Quick Sort destinations, what the app records and runs in the background, and which extra programs and gestures are on. In this order There is no fixed order here - every option works on its own. They are grouped below by the same section headers you see on the tab. Some groups, such as Wear Companion or Scheduled operations, show up only where the device or edition supports them. The elements Copy, move and overwrite behavior 1 Allow copying Allows copying files into your destination folders. Pair it with the Quick Sort destinations below to copy the current file in one tap. 2 Overwrite existing file when copying Replaces a file with the same name when copying. It applies when the destination already holds a file with the same name. Undo An overwritten file is replaced by the new one, so leave this off unless you are sure. 3 Go to next file after copying Moves on to the next file after a successful copy. It speeds up sorting a batch of files, because you do not have to navigate by hand. 4 Allow moving Allows moving files into your destination folders. Pair it with the Quick Sort destinations below to move the current file in one tap. 5 Overwrite existing file when moving Replaces a file with the same name when moving. It applies when the destination already holds a file with the same name. Undo An overwritten file is replaced by the new one, so leave this off unless you are sure. File deletion and trash 6 Enable Safe Mode Asks for confirmation before delete and move. When it is on, the app asks before deleting or moving files, to prevent accidental data loss. The two options below switch the questions separately. 7 Confirm before delete Asks before files are deleted. The Player tab has its own switch for deleting inside the player. 8 Confirm before move Asks before files are moved. Moving changes where a file lives, so the question gives you a chance to stop. 9 Use trash folder (.trash) Moves deleted files to a hidden .trash folder instead of deleting them for good. On local resources you can bring a file back with Undo before the resource is closed. Network and cloud files are always deleted permanently. On Android 12 and newer, some shared folders need the Media management permission; without it, deletion may be permanent. With the option off, files are deleted at once and the space is freed immediately. Undo The trash is a safety net, not an archive: emptying it with the Delete all in trash button removes those files for good. Quick Sort destinations 10 Max destinations (1-30) Limits how many Quick Sort destinations you can have. From 1 to 30. Each destination gets a number and a color for easy identification. 11 + Add Marks another resource as a Quick Sort destination. The button shows up once you have resources that are not destinations yet. Add resources on the main screen first, then mark them here. 12 Quick Sort destinations Your Quick Sort destinations, in the order of their numbers. Each row shows the destination's number and color, its name and its path. Use the arrows to reorder and the delete button to remove it from the list. Undo Removing a destination only unmarks the resource. The resource and its files stay where they are. Scheduled operations by schedule 13 Use scheduled operations Turns scheduled runs on or off. When it is off, nothing runs on schedule, but your operations stay saved. Switch it on and they carry on. 14 Manage scheduled operations Opens the window where you create and manage scheduled operations. A scheduled operation copies, moves or deletes files in the background on a schedule you set. App behavior and operating rules 15 Show detailed errors Shows the full error details instead of simplified messages. Useful when you are chasing a problem or reporting one. 16 Resume playback on next launch Reopens the last played file when the app starts. It continues from where you left off. 17 Remember file lists (default for new resources) Saves the file list of new resources so they open faster. After a scan the list is stored in the app database, and next time it loads at once. Use Refresh to pick up changes made outside the app. This is only the default for new resources. Photography 18 Enable photo capture Shows the camera command in the file browser. New photos are saved to the resource you are browsing. Nearby options let you ask for a file name, open the photo for editing, copy it to the clipboard, tag it with the location and choose another destination. Video recording 19 Enable video recording Shows a command to record video straight into the current resource. A second option opens the finished video in the player, and you can choose another destination folder. Voice recorder 20 Enable microphone recording Shows a microphone button in the file browser. Audio is recorded to a resource you pick or to the Downloads folder. You can also have the app ask for a file name each time. Screen recording 21 Screen video recording Records the whole screen to a video file, with sound from the microphone. A stop control and a timer appear while recording. You can choose where the video is saved. Wear Companion 22 Wear Companion Shows the watch companion in the programs panel and menu. Turn it on if you have a Wear OS watch. The companion opens from there and decides what this phone shares with the watch. Additional programs and scenarios 23 Camera OCR translation Turns on the quick photo, text recognition and translation flow. Take a photo and the app recognizes and translates its text. A second option skips the translation and shows the recognized text as it is. 24 Calculator Adds the Calculator program. It shows up in the programs menu, the quick-access panel and on the launcher desktop. 25 Stopwatch Adds the Stopwatch program. It shows up in the programs menu, the quick-access panel and on the launcher desktop. Its own settings are one row below. 26 Network Monitor Adds a diagnostic program for the network. It shows the connection, the signal and the network details. 27 System information Shows system information in the programs panel and menu. Turn it on to reach it without opening Settings. Operating system interaction 28 Prevent sleep Keeps the screen on while you use the app. While you view media files, the device does not sleep or dim during playback or viewing. 29 Auto-download incoming links Downloads a file from a link shared to the app. When you share an http(s) link to FastMediaSorter, the linked file is fetched into the resource you choose. Another option opens it in the built-in player right after a successful download; otherwise you get a short message. 30 Add widget to the Android home screen.. Lets you place an app widget on the Android home screen. Choose a widget and put it on your home screen. 31 Set as default Opens the dialog for making FastMediaSorter a default app. It has a button for each file type - images, audio, video and documents - plus two switches: show the app in Open with and handle media buttons, and accept files shared from other apps. Everything applies at once. Edge screen gestures 32 Gesture overlay Shows thin gesture strips at the screen edges, over other apps. Up to four strips, two on each side. A swipe from a strip runs the action assigned to it, such as a screenshot, the camera, the flashlight, volume or brightness, or opening an app. It needs the Display over other apps permission. 33 Configure gestures Opens the setup for edge gestures. Choose which zones are on, whether their guides are visible, and the action for each swipe direction: up, down or inward. Controls & Keybindings 34 Controls & Keybindings Opens key and button remapping for media controls. Any command can be reassigned to a D-pad button, a gamepad button, a keyboard key or a mouse button. Reset 35 Reset Management settings Returns only this tab to its defaults. Settings on the other tabs keep their values. The app asks you to confirm first. pages.title: Help - Settings: General
pages.description: General holds the settings that apply to the whole app: language and theme, the file browser, network sources, backups and caches. Come here when something should look, behave or connect differently everywhere.
pages.body: Help index / Settings: General Settings: General What this is for General holds the settings that apply to the whole app: language and theme, the file browser, network sources, backups and caches. Come here when something should look, behave or connect differently everywhere. In this order There is no fixed order here - every option works on its own. They are grouped below by the same section headers you see on the tab. The elements General interface settings 1 Language/Язык/Мова Sets the language of the whole app. Pick a language from the list and the screens switch to it. You can also choose it on the first page of the welcome wizard. 2 Color theme Chooses a light, dark or colored theme. Auto follows your device. The other options are Light, Dark, and green, blue or red variants of both. 3 Device profile Applies a ready-made set of defaults for the kind of device you use. Profiles cover a personal smartphone, tablet, TV box, car head unit, photo frame, e-book reader and more. One pick tunes many settings at once, so the app suits the device without manual work. Choose Other to keep your settings as they are. Undo Before a profile overwrites your settings, the app tells you how many it will change. Cancel keeps everything as it is. 4 Compact elements Makes everything smaller, so more fits on screen. Lists, buttons and text shrink by half. Touch targets get smaller too, so try it on a large screen first. 5 Disable animations Turns off transitions and decorative animations. Handy if animations distract you or the device feels sluggish. 6 Power saving mode Calms the app down when the battery runs low. It stops continuous animation and stops holding the screen on. Choose when it starts: never, always, or below a battery level you pick. 7 Enable Favorites Turns the Favorites feature on or off. With it on, you can mark files as favorites, see them in one list and put them on a home screen widget. The Favorites button on the main screen appears along with it. 8 Allow new windows Adds an action that opens a folder or file in a new window. The action shows up in the file browser and the player. It is useful on tablets, foldables, Chromebooks and large displays with several windows. When it is off, everything opens in the current window. Main screen interface 9 Resource grid cell size Sets how big resource tiles are in grid view. It applies to the resource list on the main screen. Smaller cells fit more resources, larger ones are easier to read. Grid view itself is switched on with the view button on the main screen. 10 Programs panel Shows the programs menu as a bar above the resource list. The bar mirrors the programs from the menu, so they are one tap away. While the panel is on, the three-dots button is hidden. File browser interface 11 Allow All Files mode Allows the All Files mode for resources. In that mode a resource shows and manages every file type, not just media: documents, archives and other files too. This switch only permits it, so you still turn it on for each resource. 12 Show hidden files Shows files and folders whose names start with a dot. Such items are normally hidden. Turn it on when you need to reach them from the file browser, and off to keep lists tidy. 13 Show subfolders separately Lists subfolders as items you can tap. Subfolders appear in the file list next to files. Tap one to go inside. 14 Swipe left action Chooses what swiping a file row to the left does. Pick an action such as open in player, send to, info, favorite, copy, move, rename, extract archive or delete, or no action at all. Actions that change files work only in folders you can write to. 15 Swipe right action Chooses what swiping a file row to the right does. Pick an action such as open in player, send to, info, favorite, copy, move, rename, extract archive or delete, or no action at all. Actions that change files work only in folders you can write to. Remote resources (SMB/(S)FTP/Cloud) 16 Local network (Ethernet) SMB Turns on connecting to shared folders on your local network. Use it for a home NAS, a Windows PC with file sharing on, or a router with a USB drive. With it on, you can add SMB resources, and the SMB tab appears on the main screen. 17 Computer on the internet (S)FTP Turns on connecting to servers over FTP and SFTP. Use it for a home server, a NAS, web hosting or a router that supports (S)FTP. With it on, you can add such resources, and the S/FTP tab appears on the main screen. 18 In cloud resources Turns on cloud storage: Google Drive, OneDrive and Dropbox. Connect an account and your cloud folders open right inside the app. With it on, the Cloud tab appears on the main screen. Share over SFTP 19 SFTP server Lets other devices open folders from this one over SFTP. Add at least one shared folder, choose password or SSH key sign-in and a port from 1024 to 65535, then turn the server on. Another device connects with the address shown here, or by scanning the pairing code in FastMediaSorter. After you change its settings, turn the server off and on again to apply them. Authorization and accounts 20 Saved authorizations Reviews the sign-ins the app saved from its web sign-in screen. The in-app web sign-in keeps cookies and logins so the app can download files from sites that need you signed in. Open this screen to remove the ones you no longer need. 21 Secure sensitive screens Hides sensitive screens from screenshots and the Recents preview. It covers screens that show passwords. They cannot be captured in a screenshot and do not appear in the Recents preview. Backups, restore and settings export 22 Export All Settings to File Saves all settings to a file. The file is FastMediaSorter_export.xml in the Downloads folder. Keep it to move your setup to another device or to return to it later. 23 Import Settings from File Loads settings from the export file. It reads FastMediaSorter_export.xml from the Downloads folder, so put the file there first - for example one exported on another device. Undo Export your current settings first if you may want to go back to them. 24 Backup settings to Google Drive Saves your settings to your Google Drive. A backup holds all settings, the resource list, network passwords and saved site sign-ins, so keep the backup file private. Cloud sign-ins for Google Drive, OneDrive and Dropbox are not included. Once a backup exists, its date and account are shown below. 25 Restore settings from Google Drive Brings settings back from your Google Drive backup. Use it on a new device or after a reset. Cloud sign-ins are not part of a backup, so sign in to Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox again afterwards. 26 SET default settings Returns all settings to their defaults. Your resources and destinations stay in place. The app asks you to confirm before it resets anything. Undo Export your settings first if you may want them back. Background sync, network and cache 27 Network Parallelism Sets how many network operations run at once. Values run from 1 to 24 and the default is 4. More at once can be faster on a fast network; fewer is gentler on a slow connection or a small server. 28 Video pre-cache size Sets how much of a streamed video is buffered ahead. Less (0.5x) saves disk space and bandwidth, but playback may stutter on a slow network. Auto lets the player decide. More (2x) plays smoother on an unstable network and uses more disk space. 29 Enable background sync Checks network resources for file changes in the background. Choose how often it checks, or run a check right away with the Sync Now button. A line below shows when the last sync happened. 30 Preload thumbnails Prepares thumbnails for network videos and PDFs after each sync. Thumbnails are made in the background, so they are ready when you open the folder. A separate option limits this to unmetered networks such as Wi-Fi. 31 Cache Size Limit Sets how much disk space the image cache may use. The cache keeps thumbnails and previews so they load fast next time. Enter a size in megabytes, or press Auto and the app picks one from the storage your device has. The default is 2 GB. 32 Clear Cache Clears the app cache to free space. It removes thumbnails, previews and temporary files downloaded from the network. The current cache size is shown next to the button, and the app asks you to confirm first. The cache fills up again as you browse. Undo Cached items are only copies, so nothing of yours is lost; the first view of a folder may just be slower. 33 Statistics collection Collects usage statistics on your device. The data stays on the device and nothing is sent automatically. While collection is on, a Statistics row appears that opens what was gathered. Tools, guides and reset 34 Downloadable Extensions Manages optional parts of the app that you download. Extensions, such as text recognition, translation or extra decoders, are downloaded only when you want them and can be deleted again to free space. 35 Permissions & Access Shows what the app may access and lets you grant it. Each permission has a short note on what it is for. Grant what you need, and open system settings for the ones Android does not let the app request on its own. 36 About system Opens a screen with information about your device and the app. It shows technical details about this device and the app. 37 User Guide Opens the online user guide in your browser. The guide opens in Russian, Ukrainian or English, depending on the app language. 38 Welcome Tutorial Opens the welcome wizard again. Go through the first-run pages once more: language, theme, device profile, network sources, capabilities and permissions. 39 Reset General section Returns only this tab to its defaults. Settings on the other tabs keep their values. The app asks you to confirm first. pages.title: Help - Duplicates
pages.description: Duplicates finds files with identical content in the resources you pick, so you can free the space the extra copies take. Open it from the file browser, in the More actions: resource menu, with Find Duplicates, or with Find and Delete Duplicates to have the extra copies removed straight after the scan.
pages.body: Help index / Duplicates Duplicates What this is for Duplicates finds files with identical content in the resources you pick, so you can free the space the extra copies take. Open it from the file browser, in the More actions: resource menu, with Find Duplicates, or with Find and Delete Duplicates to have the extra copies removed straight after the scan. In this order Open the screen from the file browser: More actions: resource, then Find Duplicates. The resource you came from is already ticked in the list 2 and stands first. Tick the other resources to search too, or untick the ones you do not need. Start Scan 3 stays off while none is ticked. Press Start Scan 3 . If a network or cloud resource is ticked, a window warns that the scan can take long and use a lot of traffic; confirm to go on. Watch the progress 4 . Cancel 5 stops the search and nothing is deleted. Read the summary 6 : how many groups of identical files were found and how much space they waste. Open a group 8 to see its copies. The app has already ticked every copy except the oldest one in each group 9 . Untick any you want to keep, or tick more. Press Delete Selected 10 and confirm. The files are deleted and the screen closes. The elements Choosing what to scan 1 Back Closes the screen; nothing is deleted by leaving. The arrow in the toolbar, the Back button of the device and the Esc key all close the screen at once. The results of a finished scan are not kept, so a new visit starts from the beginning. Shortcut Esc 2 Select resources to scan for duplicates The resources that will be searched, as chips you can tick. Each chip carries the name of a resource and its type. A tick means the resource takes part in the scan; tap a chip to switch it. Several resources can be scanned together, so a copy of a photo in two different resources is found as well. If you opened the screen from a resource's menu, that resource is ticked and listed first. 3 Start Scan Starts the search for files with identical content. The button is off until at least one resource is ticked. Files are compared by their content, not by name: first by size, then by a short piece from the start, and only the files that still match are compared completely. Empty files are ignored. For network or cloud resources a window first warns that the scan may take a long time and a lot of traffic; press OK to continue. When you came through Find and Delete Duplicates, the pre-ticked copies are deleted as soon as the scan ends, without a further question - use Find Duplicates when you want to look first. While the scan runs 4 Scan progress Shows what the scan is doing and how far it has come. The stage appears in capital letters: LISTING while the files are collected, QUICK_HASH while the starts of equal-sized files are compared, and FULL_HASH while the remaining candidates are compared completely. Below it a counter shows the number of files processed out of the total. 5 Cancel Stops the scan and brings you back to the list of resources. Nothing is deleted by cancelling. You can change the ticked resources and start again. Results and deletion 6 Result summary How many groups of identical files were found and how much space is wasted. The line reads, for example, Found 12 groups, then Wasted space and a size. Wasted space counts every copy except one per group, so it is the amount you can free. 7 Duplicate groups One row per set of identical files. Each group is a set of files with the same content. A group always holds at least two files. Scroll the list to go through all groups. 8 Group header Names the group and opens or closes its copies. The title is the name of one file of the group, and the line under it gives the size of one file and the number of files. Tap the header to expand the group and see where each copy lies; all groups start collapsed. 9 File row with checkbox One copy: its name, its full path and a checkbox that marks it for deletion. Tap the row or its checkbox to tick or untick the copy. A ticked copy is deleted when you press Delete Selected. Dragging a finger down along the checkboxes of one group ticks a whole range at once and never unticks. The app does not stop you from ticking every copy of a group, so keep at least one copy unticked. The row cannot open the file; use the path to find it in the file browser. 10 Delete Selected Deletes all ticked copies after you confirm. The button appears as soon as at least one copy is ticked and shows how many files will go and how much space they take. A confirmation window with Delete and Cancel repeats the number and says the deletion cannot be undone. After deleting, a short message tells you the files are gone and the screen closes. Undo The selected files are lost. They stay in a hidden .trash folder of their resource only when Use trash folder (.trash) is switched on in Settings and the files are local ones that can be moved there; network and cloud files, and everything with the trash off, are deleted for good. Restoring from a backup is then the only way back. 11 No duplicates found. Tells you that no identical files were found. It appears when the scan has finished and there are no groups: nothing to delete in the chosen resources. Go back and pick other resources to search more. pages.title: Help - Front flashlight
pages.description: The front flashlight turns the whole screen into a lamp: a lit field in the color you choose, at the brightness you choose, with a clock on it. Use it as a light in a dark room.
pages.body: Help index / Front flashlight Front flashlight What this is for The front flashlight turns the whole screen into a lamp: a lit field in the color you choose, at the brightness you choose, with a clock on it. Use it as a light in a dark room. In this order Open Front flashlight from the programs menu, the programs panel or a home-screen widget. If it is not offered, switch it on first in Settings, on the Management tab, in the group Additional programs and scenarios. The whole screen 1 lights up at full brightness. Press Light color 3 if white is not what you need, pick a color in the palette 6 and confirm with OK 8 . The choice is remembered for next time. Set the brightness with one of the five steps 4 , or swipe up or down anywhere on the screen. Both move the same five steps. The clock 2 shows the time while the lamp is on, so you do not need to switch it off to check. Tap an empty spot of the screen 1 to close the lamp. With a keyboard or a D-pad, press Enter. The elements The lit screen 1 Lit screen The whole window glows in the color you chose, so the screen works as a lamp. The glow covers the entire window, also the areas behind the camera cutout and the system bars, and the screen stays awake for as long as the lamp is open. Only the brightness of this window is raised, never the brightness setting of the phone, so closing the lamp leaves the phone exactly as bright as it was. A short tap on an empty spot closes the lamp. A swipe up or down changes the brightness; a sideways swipe does nothing. If one of the controls has the focus, Enter presses that control instead of closing. Shortcut Enter / D-pad center 2 Clock Shows the time on the glow, a quarter of the way down. The time is drawn in black and moves on at the start of every minute. Whether it reads in 12 or 24 hours follows the unit system of the app (Metric shows 24 hours, US shows 12), not the clock format of the device. It is only a display: a tap on it closes the lamp like a tap anywhere else. Light controls 3 Light color Chooses another color for the light. Opens the dialog with a palette of colors. The first time the light is white; after that the lamp opens in the color you picked last. A warm yellow is easy for reading, and a red keeps your eyes used to the dark. 4 Brightness steps Five steps from dim to full light, one tap each. Tap a step to set the brightness; the step the window is lit at is highlighted. The lowest step is dim but not black, so the screen never looks switched off. A swipe up or down anywhere on the screen moves through the same five steps: up is brighter, down is dimmer, and one sweep across the whole height covers the full range. The lamp always opens at the brightest step, because the brightness is not remembered. Select Color dialog 5 Current color Shows the color you are about to apply, with its name. The square and the name next to it change as soon as you tap a color in the palette. Nothing reaches the lamp until you press OK. 6 Color palette Thirty ready colors to choose from. Tap a color to select it: a check mark marks the choice and the preview above follows. You can try as many as you like before you confirm. The palette holds reds, blues, greens, yellows and oranges, earth tones, grays, black and white. 7 Cancel Closes the dialog and keeps the color the lamp already has. Nothing changes: the lamp keeps the color it had before you opened the dialog. Shortcut Esc 8 OK Applies the selected color to the lamp. The glow changes at once and the color is saved, so the lamp opens in it next time. The button has the focus when the dialog opens, so with a keyboard one press of Enter is enough. pages.title: Help - Kryvavitsa and the Monster
pages.description: A small turn-based puzzle on a grid. Lead the blue Monster to the green exit before the red Kryvavitsa and her purple helpers corner you: you move one cell per turn, the enemies answer after each move, and every level is a bigger board.
pages.body: Help index / Kryvavitsa and the Monster Kryvavitsa and the Monster What this is for A small turn-based puzzle on a grid. Lead the blue Monster to the green exit before the red Kryvavitsa and her purple helpers corner you: you move one cell per turn, the enemies answer after each move, and every level is a bigger board. In this order Open the game from the programs menu, the programs panel, the launcher or a home-screen widget. It is off after installation, so switch Mini-game on first in Settings, on the Management tab, in the group Additional programs and scenarios. The game saves itself and continues where you left it. The first time, press How to play? 11 : its own screen shows what every color on the board means and the rules. Move one cell per turn on the board 5 : swipe anywhere on it, tap the side of the Monster where you want to go, press the arrows 6 , or use the keyboard or a D-pad. After each move the enemies move too. Push gray walls into free cells to clear a path. If an enemy ends up on your cell or next to it, the level is lost. Next turn 7 skips your step while the enemies still move, for the moments when standing still is safer than moving. Reaching the exit gives +1000 and the next level starts by itself after a second, or at once with Next level 8 . Level 2 , Score 3 and Turns 4 keep count above the board. If a level goes wrong, Restart level 9 starts it again on a fresh board for 500 points; Reset 8 throws the whole game away and starts from level 1. Mode 10 changes how the board looks. The elements Top bar and counters 1 Back Leaves the game and returns to where you came from. The game saves itself after every move, so leaving does not lose your place: when you open the game again it continues with the same level, score and turns. The Back button of the device does the same. Shortcut Esc 2 Level Shows which level you are on. You start at level 1. The board grows as the level goes up - 8 by 8 cells at first, one cell more every third level, up to 20 by 20 - and more purple enemies appear on it. 3 Score Your points: moves cost, pushes and the exit pay. Every turn costs 10 points, also a skipped one. Pushing a wall gives +10, crushing a purple enemy +50 and reaching the exit +1000. The score never goes below zero. Restarting a level costs 500 points. 4 Turns How many turns you have played in this game. A step and a skipped turn both count. The number keeps growing from level to level and starts again from zero only when you reset the game. Board and moves 5 Game board The playing field: the Monster, the exit, the enemies and the walls. Blue is the Monster you control, green is the exit, red is the Kryvavitsa that hunts you, purple are her lesser helpers that wander at random, gray blocks are walls you can push, and the thick border cannot be crossed. A swipe in any direction, or a tap above, below or beside the Monster, moves it one cell that way; a tap right on the Monster does nothing. When you are caught, a line joins you to the enemy and a short message appears. 6 Arrow buttons Four buttons that move the Monster one cell up, down, left or right. They do the same as a swipe or a tap on the board, which makes them handy when you prefer buttons or play with one hand. A move into the border or into a wall that cannot be pushed is refused and costs nothing. The keyboard works too: the arrow keys, W A S D or the numeric keypad. Shortcut Arrow keys / W, A, S, D / Numpad 8, 4, 2, 6 7 Next turn Lets the enemies move while the Monster stays where it is. It counts as a turn and costs 10 points, like a step. Use it when every step would bring you next to an enemy and waiting is safer. Game actions 8 Reset Starts the next step of the game: a new game, the next level, or a restart after a defeat. Its label follows the situation. While you are playing it reads Reset and starts a brand new game from level 1, with score and turns at zero, without asking. After you reach the exit it reads Next level and moves on to the next board. After you were caught it reads Restart level and tries the same level again on a fresh board. Undo Reset throws away the level, score and turns of the running game, and there is no way back to them - only a new game from level 1. Restart level after a defeat costs 500 points. Shortcut Enter / Space / D-pad center 9 Restart level Starts the current level over on a fresh board when you are stuck. The level number stays, the board is generated again, and the price is the same as being caught: 500 points, never taking the score below zero. The button is shown only while a level is running; after a defeat the main button takes this label and does the same. Undo The current board and 500 points are lost, and the old board does not come back. Shortcut R 10 Game mode Changes how the board looks: Classic, Kryvavitsa or Contrast. The button carries the name of the current mode. Press it to open the list Game mode and pick another one. Classic draws colored balls, Kryvavitsa draws figures - a man, a woman with a machine gun, women with knives, a door - and Contrast uses solid tiles in the classic colors. Only the look changes: the rules, your position and your score stay as they are. The choice is remembered. 11 How to play? Opens the game's own help screen with the legend and the rules. The screen is called How to play and has its own Back button. It tells the goal, shows what each color or figure on the board means (it follows the mode you chose) and lists the rules and the score. Close it to return to your game exactly as it was. pages.title: Help - Controls & Keybindings
pages.description: Choose which key, gamepad button or mouse button runs each command - playback, navigation, sorting and browsing. Every command comes with a factory key, so you change only what you want, and you can put it back whenever you like.
pages.body: Help index / Controls & Keybindings Controls & Keybindings What this is for Choose which key, gamepad button or mouse button runs each command - playback, navigation, sorting and browsing. Every command comes with a factory key, so you change only what you want, and you can put it back whenever you like. In this order Open Controls & Keybindings from Settings, on the Management tab. The commands are grouped by purpose, and the groups start folded. Find the command: type part of its name in the search field 2 , or tap a group title 3 to open the group. Press Edit binding 6 on the command's row 5 and pick the device whose key you want to change - Keyboard, Gamepad and so on. A window opens 9 and waits. Press the new key or button within the time shown 10 and check what was caught 11 . If a red message says the key is taken 12 , press another one or Cancel 13 . Otherwise press Set 14 to save it. To go back to the factory key, use the reset on the row 7 for one command, the group reset 4 for a whole group, or Reset All 8 for everything. The last two ask first. Changes are saved the moment you make them. Back 1 leaves the screen. The elements Top bar and search 1 Back Leaves the screen and returns to Settings. There is nothing to confirm: every change is already saved when you make it. 2 Search commands.. Narrows the list to the commands that match. Type part of a command name, such as Next File, or of a key name, and the list shrinks as you type. A group with no match disappears. A folded group with a match shows only its title, so tap it to see the matching rows. Clear the field to bring everything back. Groups and commands 3 Command groups Folds and unfolds the commands of one group. Commands are grouped by purpose: Playback, Navigation, View & Zoom, Audio & Subtitles, System UI, Sorting Actions, Operation shortcuts, Browser Actions and, only in builds with a VR runtime, VR Only. Groups start folded; tap a title to open one. The app remembers which groups you left open. On a wide window the rows are set in two columns. 4 Reset Group Puts one group back to its factory keys. This is the small round-arrow icon at the end of a group title. The app asks whether to reset all bindings in that group to factory defaults, and changes nothing until you press Reset. Only the keys you changed in that group are affected. Undo Your own keys in that group are lost and the factory ones return. To get a key back, assign it again with Edit binding. 5 Command row A command and the keys that run it. The command name is on top. Below it are its current keys, each with a mark for the device - keyboard, gamepad, mouse or VR; a dash means no key is set. One command can have keys on several devices at once, so a gamepad button and a keyboard key can do the same thing. 6 Edit binding Gives this command a new key or button. A small menu asks which device to change. Keyboard and Gamepad are always offered, each with its current key or (not set); Mouse and VR appear only when the command already has a key for them. After you pick one, the key capture window opens. The new key takes the place of the old one for that device. 7 Reset to default Puts this one command back to its factory key. It works only for a command you have changed; for an untouched command the button is dimmed. It happens at once, without a question. Undo Your own key for this command is lost and the factory key returns. Assign it again with Edit binding if you want it back. Reset everything 8 Reset All Puts every command back to its factory keys. The app asks Reset every binding to factory defaults? This cannot be undone., and nothing changes until you press Reset. Afterwards each command uses its original keyboard, gamepad and mouse buttons. Undo All your own keys are lost at once and cannot be restored. Assign them again one by one. Key capture window 9 Press a key or button.. Tells you the app is waiting for your key. The window covers the screen and listens for a keyboard key (with Ctrl, Shift or Alt if you hold them), a gamepad button, a stick, trigger or D-pad push, or a mouse button. The system Back key is not taken as a new key. 10 Countdown Shows how many seconds are left to press a key. You have 30 seconds. When the time runs out, the window closes on its own and nothing is changed. 11 Captured key Shows the key or button the app caught. It reads Captured: and the name of what you pressed, for example Ctrl+Shift+K for a keyboard key with modifiers. Before you press anything it shows a dash. If the first press was not what you meant, press another key - the last one counts. 12 Conflict message Warns that another command already uses this key. A red line reads Already bound to: and the names of those commands. While it is shown, Set stays off, so two commands cannot share one key. Press a different key, or cancel and free the other command first. 13 Cancel Closes the window and changes nothing. The command keeps its old key. Use it when you opened the window by mistake or the key you wanted is already taken. 14 Set Saves the caught key for this command. The button works only after a key was caught and no other command uses it. It saves the key right away, closes the window and updates the row. pages.title: Help - Edit panel
pages.description: Choose what the Quick launch panel shows. The panel has fifteen fixed places; here you fill each one with an app, a tool of FastMediaSorter, one of your resources or an Android settings screen, and you can swap them around or clear them.
pages.body: Help index / Edit panel Edit panel What this is for Choose what the Quick launch panel shows. The panel has fifteen fixed places; here you fill each one with an app, a tool of FastMediaSorter, one of your resources or an Android settings screen, and you can swap them around or clear them. In this order You get here from the Edit button of the Quick launch panel, by tapping a free place on it, or from the edge gesture settings. The grid 3 shows the panel as it is now. Tap a free place 5 or any tile 4 . The Add to panel window 9 asks what kind of shortcut you want: an Android app, a FastMediaSorter feature, a FastMediaSorter resource or an Android setting. A list of that kind opens (11 to 14). Tap the item you want and it goes into the place at once. A short list has no search field; a long one gets it 10 . To change a tile that is already there, long-press it: Move 6 swaps it with another place, Replace 7 opens the same kind choice again, Remove 8 empties the place. Reset panel 2 puts the factory set back after you confirm. Back 1 leaves the screen - every change is saved as you make it. The elements Top bar 1 Back Leaves the screen and returns to the panel. There is nothing to save: each change is stored as soon as you make it, and the panel shows it the next time it opens. 2 Reset panel Puts the panel back to the set it had after installation. The app asks Reset panel? and explains that the panel returns to the default set of apps and shortcuts created at install. Nothing changes until you confirm. The factory set is FastMediaSorter first, then its own tools that exist in your edition, one of your resources and Android Settings, with the last places left free. Undo All your own tiles are lost and the factory set returns. To get a tile back, add it again. Tile grid 3 Tile grid The fifteen fixed places of the panel. The grid has three columns in a narrow window and five in a wide one, the same as the panel. The number of places cannot be changed. Every place is either a tile with an icon and a name or a free place with a plus. The grid takes keyboard and D-pad focus when the screen opens. 4 Tile A shortcut that is already on the panel. Tap it to replace it: the Add to panel window opens for the same place, and whatever you pick takes its spot. Long-press it for the menu with Move, Replace and Remove. The icon shows what the tile opens: an app keeps its own icon, and tools and settings have theirs. 5 Empty - tap to add A free place waiting for a shortcut. Tap it, or long-press it - both do the same here - and the Add to panel window opens. The place stays free until you pick something. Tile menu (long press) 6 Move Moves a tile to another place. A list of places numbered from 1 to 15 opens. Pick the number you want. If that place already has a tile, the two tiles swap; if it is free, the tile just moves there. Cancel leaves everything where it was. 7 Replace Puts something else into the same place. Opens the same Add to panel window as a tap on the tile. The new choice takes the place of the old one; the old tile is not kept. 8 Remove Empties the place. The tile is taken off the panel at once, without a question, and the place becomes free again. The app, tool or resource it pointed to is not touched. Undo The tile cannot be brought back with an undo button. Add it again from the free place, or use Reset panel to get the factory set. Add to panel window 9 Add to panel Asks what kind of shortcut should go into this place. A short list with four choices: Android app, FastMediaSorter feature, FastMediaSorter resource and Android OS settings. Each opens its own list. Cancel closes the window and changes nothing. The same window opens for Replace. 10 Type to search Narrows a long list as you type. The field has a clear button and appears only when the list is longer than the window; a short list shows no field. Type part of a name and the rows narrow as you go. If nothing matches, the list says Nothing found. It works the same way in all four lists below. 11 Choose an app Lists the apps you can pin as a tile. Shows the apps installed on this phone that can be launched, sorted by name and each with its own icon. Tap one and it goes into the place. If you later remove that app from the phone, its tile opens nothing. 12 Choose a feature Lists tools and screens of FastMediaSorter itself. Shows what exists in your edition, for example the calculator, the stopwatch, the network monitor, the mini-game, Streams and Favorites; the tools come first and the rest follow. A tool that is switched off in Settings stays in the list with the note Off - tap to turn on; as a tile it opens the matching setting instead of the tool. Features that are not part of your edition are not listed. 13 Choose Android OS setting Lists Android settings screens you can pin. Shows only the screens this phone can really open: Settings, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Display, Sound, Battery, Storage, App info, Date and time and, where your phone has them, Developer options, Battery saver, Auto-rotate, Accessibility, Wireless networks, Data usage, NFC, VPN, Location and Hotspot. A screen your phone does not have is simply missing. 14 Choose a resource Lists your resources you can pin. Shows your resources by name, each with the icon of its type, such as a device folder, a network share or a cloud folder. One tile points to one resource; tapping the tile on the panel later opens that resource in the file browser. pages.title: Help - Settings: Media
pages.description: Media is where you decide which kinds of files the app handles and how each kind behaves: images, video, audio, documents, translation, streams and live broadcasting.
headings: Text, PDF, EPUB and Office viewing
pages.body: Help index / Settings: Media Settings: Media What this is for Media is where you decide which kinds of files the app handles and how each kind behaves: images, video, audio, documents, translation, streams and live broadcasting. In this order There is no fixed order here - every option works on its own. The tab folds into groups, one per kind of media, and each group lists its options below. Some groups, such as Streams and Broadcast, show up only in editions that include them. The elements Images, GIFs and slideshow 1 Support static images Lets the app view static images. JPG, PNG, WEBP, HEIC and other image formats become viewable. Turn it off if you never use the app for pictures. 2 Support GIF animation Plays animated GIFs in the file browser and player. Turn it on to see GIFs move. The same page also sets size limits for images and animations. 3 Load images at full resolution Loads original-resolution images so you can zoom in. It enables pinch-to-zoom and rotation gestures in command panel mode, but uses more data and memory. By default the app loads images at 1920 px; over the network, the original is downloaded for zooming, which is slower. 4 Crop images to fill screen Fills the whole screen when image and device orientation match. In fullscreen and slideshow, a landscape image on a landscape screen (or portrait on portrait) is cropped to fill it. With the option off, every image fits inside the screen without cropping. 5 Dynamic Background Extension Fills the empty bars around an image with its own edge colors. It softens letterboxing and pillarboxing when an image does not match the screen shape. Plain backgrounds get a uniform fill; busier ones get streaks that continue the picture. 6 Play music during slideshow Plays music while a slideshow runs. Tracks from the resource you choose play in random order during image and GIF slideshows. Pick a resource that holds your music; the picker appears when the option is on. 7 Set as default image viewer Makes FastMediaSorter the app that opens your images. Android shows its own dialog: pick FastMediaSorter and tap Always. This is not permanent - Android keeps the choice in its own settings, and you can change it back there. Video and player settings 8 Support video Lets the app play video. MP4, MKV, MOV, WEBM and other video formats become playable in the built-in player. 9 Show video thumbnails Shows a preview frame for each video in the file browser. The first frame of the video becomes its thumbnail. For network files it can take two seconds or more, because the file has to be downloaded and processed first. 10 Open video files in fullscreen mode Starts videos from the file browser in fullscreen. A video you open from the file browser goes straight into fullscreen playback. 11 Save video frames to clipboard Also copies each extracted video frame to the clipboard. When you extract a frame from a video, it also goes to the clipboard, ready to paste. 12 Set as default video player Makes FastMediaSorter the app that plays your videos. Android shows its own dialog: pick FastMediaSorter and tap Always. This is not permanent - Android keeps the choice in its own settings, and you can change it back there. Audio playback, covers and visuals 13 Support audio Lets the app play audio. MP3, FLAC, AAC, OGG and other audio formats become playable. 14 Search audio covers online Looks online for covers of tracks that have none embedded. Covers are downloaded from the internet. A Search only on Wi-Fi option appears next to it, so mobile data stays untouched. 15 Show random photos during audio playback Shows random photos while audio plays. Photos come from the resource you pick, one random photo per song. Only still images are used; videos are ignored. 16 Visualizer when no cover art Chooses what the player shows for a track without cover art. Pick a plain black background, a music note with pulse rings, breathing bars, waves and particles, or a visualization video. 17 Set as default audio player Makes FastMediaSorter the app that plays your music. Android shows its own dialog: pick FastMediaSorter and tap Always. This is not permanent - Android keeps the choice in its own settings, and you can change it back there. Text, PDF, EPUB and Office viewing 18 Support text files (.txt, .md, .log, .json, .xml) Lets the app open plain text files. That covers .txt, .md, .log, .json and .xml files. 19 Support PDF documents Opens PDF files in the built-in viewer. There is also a separate option for large PDF thumbnails; it is slower. 20 Support EPUB e-books Reads EPUB e-books. The reader has bookmarks and a table of contents. 21 Support Office documents Opens Office documents with another app. DOC, DOCX, RTF and ODT open in an external app, not in FastMediaSorter itself. 22 Set as default document viewer Makes FastMediaSorter the app that opens your documents. Android shows its own dialog: pick FastMediaSorter and tap Always. This is not permanent - Android keeps the choice in its own settings, and you can change it back there. Translation, digitization (OCR) 23 Enable text recognition Turns on text recognition for images and PDFs. Text is extracted so you can copy it. The font size and font family for the recognized text are set just below. 24 Enable Translation Turns on translation of text recognized in images. The visible text is translated from the original language into the one you choose below. Translation packs can be installed from the downloads row. 25 Original Language Chooses the language of the text you want to translate. The swap button between the two language fields flips them in one tap. 26 Translate To Chooses the language to translate into. Translations appear in this language. When you need the other direction, swap the two languages with the button between them. 27 OCR & translation downloads Opens the downloads for text recognition and translation. Install the OCR and translation packs you need, and remove them again to free space. Streams 28 Enable Streams Turns on internet audio, video and RTSP streams. Streams add a channel catalog and playback for online radio and television. The options below tune how they behave. 29 Default order Chooses the default order of the channel list. Order by name, topic, language, country or recently added. 30 Show by default Chooses which channels show by default. All channels, only audio, or only video. 31 Updating the channel list Decides when the channel list gets updated. Choose between updating only when you ask, a suggestion when you open Streams, or automatic updates on Wi-Fi. 32 Audio language for streams Picks the audio language streams start with. Choose Default, English, Russian or Ukrainian. 33 Subtitle language for streams Picks the subtitle language streams start with. Choose Default, English, Russian or Ukrainian. 34 Ultra-smart stream buffering Gives streams a bigger start-up cushion. Streams start with a bigger buffer and reconnect quietly when the connection is shaky. 35 Play casts at once Starts a cast from another device without asking. Normally a cast your other device sends here waits for you to accept it. With this on, it starts playing right away. 36 Enable Picture-in-Picture Adds a Picture-in-Picture button to the player. The player also enters Picture-in-Picture on its own when you press Home (Android 12 and newer). 37 Clear play marks Clears the green and red play marks on all channels. The channels themselves stay. The app asks you to confirm first. Undo Only the marks are removed; the channels stay where they are. Broadcast 38 Enable live broadcasting Allows live audio broadcasting from this device. With it on, broadcast shortcuts appear in the app. The options below set the title, port, sound quality and microphone behavior. 39 Broadcast title Names your broadcast. This is the name your broadcast goes by. The default is Phone Broadcast. 40 Port Sets the network port for the broadcast. The app accepts ports from 1 to 65535. Change it only if you have a reason, for example another app that already uses the current port. 41 Bit rate Sets the sound quality of the broadcast. Choose 128, 192, 256 or 320 kbps. Higher means better sound and more data. 42 Audio format Sets the sample rate and the number of channels. Choose 44.1 or 48 kHz, in mono or stereo. 43 Microphone gain Sets how loud your microphone is in the broadcast. Choose from 50% to 400%. 100% leaves the level unchanged. 44 Feedback guard Prevents the squeal when a listener nearby plays the broadcast aloud. It turns the microphone gain down when the broadcast is played aloud close to the microphone, so the sound cannot build up. 45 Auto-open share screen Opens the share screen when a broadcast starts. You do not have to open it yourself. Reset 46 Reset Media section Returns only this tab to its defaults. Settings on the other tabs keep their values. The app asks you to confirm first. pages.title: Help - Quick launch
pages.description: Quick launch is a pop-up grid of fifteen tiles that opens over whatever you are doing. One tap starts an app, a tool of FastMediaSorter, one of your resources or an Android settings screen, and the panel closes.
pages.body: Help index / Quick launch Quick launch What this is for Quick launch is a pop-up grid of fifteen tiles that opens over whatever you are doing. One tap starts an app, a tool of FastMediaSorter, one of your resources or an Android settings screen, and the panel closes. In this order Open the panel in one of three ways: the Quick Settings tile 7 , an edge swipe 8 or the Programs menu 9 . Tap a tile 5 to start what it points to. The panel closes by itself, so you land straight in the app or screen you picked. A dimmed tile with a plus 6 is a free place. Tap it to choose what goes there. Press Edit 3 to rearrange the panel, replace tiles or put it back to the factory set. Press Close 1 , tap outside the panel or use Back to dismiss it without starting anything. The elements Panel header 1 Close Closes the panel and returns you to what you were doing. The panel floats over the app that was on the screen, so closing it simply takes it away. Tapping outside the panel or pressing Back does the same. 2 Quick launch Names the panel. Quick launch is the name of the panel here, on the Quick Settings tile and in the Programs menu, so you recognize it wherever you open it from. 3 Edit Opens the screen where you choose what is on the panel. The Edit panel screen lets you fill a free place, replace a tile, move it, remove it or reset the panel to the factory set. Your changes show on the panel at once when you come back. Tile grid 4 Tile grid Fifteen fixed places for your shortcuts. The grid always has fifteen places: three columns in a narrow window and five in a wide one. You cannot add more places, but any of them can be filled, replaced, moved or emptied in Edit panel. The first time the panel opens, the app fills it in for you: FastMediaSorter first, then its own tools that exist in your edition, one of your resources and the Android settings, with the last few places left free for your own apps. Tiles 5 Tile Starts the app, tool, resource or settings screen it shows. Tap a tile and the panel launches its target, then closes. A tile can point to an Android app, a FastMediaSorter tool such as the calculator, the mini-game, Streams or Favorites, one of your resources (it opens in the file browser) or an Android settings screen. If a tool is switched off in Settings, the tile opens the matching setting, where there is one, instead of doing nothing. A Wi-Fi or Bluetooth tile switches the radio right away in editions that can do it, and otherwise opens the matching Android screen. If a tile points to an app that has been removed, nothing opens and the panel just closes. 6 Empty - tap to add A free place waiting for your shortcut. The place is shown dimmed with a plus. Tapping it does not close the panel: it opens the Edit panel screen, where you choose what goes into that place. Ways to open the panel 7 Quick Settings tile A Quick launch tile in the Android quick settings. Pull down the Android quick settings, tap its Edit button and drag the Quick launch tile in. Tapping the tile closes the shade and opens the panel over the app underneath. It is available in every edition on Android 7 and later, so it works even where edge swipes are not offered. 8 Edge swipe A swipe from the screen edge opens the panel. In the edge gesture settings, give one swipe direction the action Open quick-access panel. Edge gestures need the gesture overlay turned on in Settings and are offered in the Standard and noLegal editions; in these editions an upward swipe in the upper left band is already set to open the panel on first start. The panel then appears over the current app, with no screenshot and no extra prompts. 9 Programs menu The Quick launch entry of the main screen's programs. On the main screen, Quick launch is always in the list of programs - there is no switch for it. You find the list in the programs panel, or under More actions when that panel is off. Choosing the entry opens the panel. pages.title: Help - Mirror
pages.description: The mirror shows the front camera full screen inside a bright field that lights your face, like the lamp around a make-up mirror. Use it to check your face or hair, and to take a quick photo or video of yourself.
pages.body: Help index / Mirror Mirror What this is for The mirror shows the front camera full screen inside a bright field that lights your face, like the lamp around a make-up mirror. Use it to check your face or hair, and to take a quick photo or video of yourself. In this order Open Mirror from the programs menu, the programs panel or a launcher shortcut. It is switched on by default on a phone with a front camera. The first time, allow the camera when asked. Your picture 1 appears inside the bright field 2 . Choose how close you want to be with the zoom buttons 6 . The mirror opens at 2x the first time and afterwards at the step you used last. Switch the bright field off and on with the Front flashlight button 4 if the light is too strong or you do not need it. Press Flip image 5 to switch between the mirror view and the view other people have of you. Take a photo with 7 , or start and stop a video with 8 . The first video asks for the microphone. Press Close mirror 3 when you are done. The camera is released at once. The elements Picture and light 1 Mirror picture Your face from the front camera, shown the way a real mirror shows it. The front camera fills the screen. At first the picture is flipped sideways like a mirror, so left is left as you see yourself. The screen stays awake while the mirror is open. The camera permission is asked on the first entry. If you refuse, the mirror closes with the message that it cannot open. On a device without a front camera it does not open at all. 2 Bright field A white frame around the picture that lights your face. While the backlight is on, the window is raised to full brightness and the white field around the picture works like the lamp around a make-up mirror. Only the brightness of this window is raised, never the brightness setting of the phone. With the backlight off the field disappears and the window returns to the brightness your phone normally has. Controls in the corners 3 Close mirror Leaves the mirror and lets go of the camera. It sits in the top-left corner. If a video is being recorded, the recording is stopped and still saved. The zoom, the flip and the backlight are remembered for the next time. 4 Front flashlight Switches the bright white field on and off without leaving the screen. The field is on by default. With it on, the window is at full brightness and your face is lit; with it off, the screen around the picture is black and the phone uses its normal brightness. Your choice is remembered. The button carries the name of the Front flashlight program, because the field is the same idea: the screen as a lamp. 5 Flip image Swaps between the mirror view and the view other people have of you. At first you see yourself as in a mirror, with left and right swapped. Press the button to see the picture the other way round, the way a camera shows you to others; press again to go back. Only what you see changes: photos and videos are saved as the camera captured them. The choice is remembered. 6 Zoom presets Four buttons, 1x, 2x, 3x and 5x, bring your face closer. The active step is shown in bold with inverted colors. The mirror opens at 2x the first time, and afterwards at the step you used last. On most front cameras every step above 1x is digital, so the picture gets coarser as the number grows. The zoom stays when you start a recording. Photo and video 7 Take photo Takes a photo of what the front camera sees. The photo is saved in the folder you chose for the photos of the in-app camera. If you chose none, or the chosen resource is not a folder on the device, it goes to the Camera folder of the phone. A short message confirms the save. The button is grayed out while a shot is being saved, so a double press does no harm. A photo taken with the phone on its side is saved the right way up. 8 Record video Starts and stops a video recording from the front camera. The first press starts the recording and the button turns into a recording symbol; press it again to stop. The first recording asks for the microphone; if you refuse, the video is recorded without sound. After stopping, the button waits for a moment while the file is finished, and then a message confirms the save. The video goes to the folder chosen for video recording, or to the Camera folder of the phone when none is chosen or the chosen resource is not a folder on the device. pages.title: Help - My devices
pages.description: My devices holds the exchange servers that link all your own devices - phone, computer, watch, TV box. Once this phone is signed in to one, it can see the folders and broadcasts your other devices share, and they can see yours; the server only passes them along.
headings: Devices of an account (tap a card)
Sign in to an exchange server window
pages.body: Help index / My devices My devices What this is for My devices holds the exchange servers that link all your own devices - phone, computer, watch, TV box. Once this phone is signed in to one, it can see the folders and broadcasts your other devices share, and they can see yours; the server only passes them along. In this order Open My devices from Settings, on the General tab (the row is there in editions with network sources). With no server yet, a short message 2 says so; press Add server 5 to begin. In the sign-in window, bring in the server's connection string by pasting, scanning or choosing a file 21 , then check the address 22 and type your login 23 and password 24 . If the other device gave you a pairing code, tick 25 and enter the code instead of the password, then press Sign in 26 . Read What the server can see 4 once, so you know what the server learns and what stays encrypted on your devices. Each server you add becomes a card in the list 3 : its address, your login and the state of the link, such as Connected with the number of devices. Tap a card to see the devices of that account 18 . To bring a new device in without typing the password there, issue a pairing code 20 ; to remove a device you no longer use, press Revoke 19 . The three dots on a card (9 to 17) hold the rest: change the address, make this server the outgoing one, connect a watch, pass the server on, sign out, and more. The three buttons at the bottom (6, 7, 8) open pages of the project website about adding a server, the server itself and connecting a watch. The elements The list of servers 1 My devices The title bar of the screen, with the way back. The arrow returns to the previous screen. Here a device is any phone, computer, watch or TV box that is signed in to the same account on an exchange server, and one account can sit on one server only. This screen lists those servers; the devices themselves are shown when you tap a card. 2 Empty list message Tells you that there is no exchange server yet. It shows only while the list has no cards. It says that adding a server lets you see the resources and broadcasts of all your devices; Add server below is the way to do it. 3 Server cards One card per exchange server you are signed in to. A card shows the server's address, your login on it and a status line: Checking the connection.., Connected with the number of devices, or a short note about what is wrong - for example that the server does not answer or that this phone was signed out. Cards marked Outgoing are the server through which this phone publishes its folders and broadcasts. Tap a card to open the list of devices in that account; the three dots on the card open its menu. 4 What the server can see A plain statement of what the exchange server learns and what it cannot read. The server sees the names of your account, devices, folders and broadcasts, which devices are online, and how much is sent and when. It cannot open what goes through it: folders and their files, broadcasts and the clipboard are encrypted on your device and opened only on your other devices or by people you gave access to. To look inside, whoever runs the server would have to add a device of their own to your account, and it would appear in your list of devices. 5 Add server Signs this phone in to an exchange server. It opens the Sign in to an exchange server window. You need the server's connection string, or its address, and a login with a password or a pairing code. Nothing is saved until you press Sign in and the server accepts you. Afterwards the server appears as a card in the list. Pages of the project website 6 About adding a server Opens a page of the project website about adding a server. The page walks through the pairing code and the connection string. It opens in your browser. 7 About the exchange server Opens a page of the project website about the exchange server. It explains who runs a server, how it connects your devices without opening a router, and what it sees and keeps. It opens in your browser. 8 About connecting a watch Opens a page of the project website about connecting a watch. The button shows only in editions that have the Wear companion, the same editions in which a card menu offers Connect watch. The page opens in your browser. Server card menu (three dots) 9 Change address Changes the address of a server without signing in again. A small window shows the address as host and port. If the server has announced a different address, the window mentions it and offers Use the announced address. Save moves your sign-in to the new address. If an entry with that address and login already exists, or the sign-in could not be moved, nothing is changed and a message says so. 10 Make outgoing Makes this server the one through which this phone shares. This phone publishes its folders and broadcasts through one server at a time. Choosing this server moves publishing here and marks the card Outgoing. If the previous server could not be reached, publishing stops on this phone anyway and a message says that the share may stay listed there for a while. The item is hidden on the card that is already outgoing. 11 Connect watch Signs your watch in to this server. The phone hands the watch a one-time code, so you type no password on the watch. Keep the watch near, unlocked and connected. The item appears only in editions with the Wear companion, and a message says if the companion is off, no watch is connected, or the watch did not answer. 12 Pass the server on Shows a code that tells another device where this server is. A window shows a QR code and a text. Send passes the text to another app and Copy puts it on the clipboard. The text carries the address and the certificate of the server, never your login or password, so the other device still needs its own sign-in. 13 Attach everything automatically Adds every new folder of this account to this phone without asking. With the check mark on, a folder that one of your devices starts sharing appears in your resources by itself. It is off until you turn it on. Tap the item again to turn it off. 14 Sign in again Opens the sign-in window with this server already filled in. Use it when the card says that you were signed out or the sign-in was revoked, or on a new phone after a backup restore. The address, the server's certificate and your login are filled in; you type the password once. The same entry is renewed, so nothing is duplicated. 15 Change password Changes the password of your account on this server. You enter the current password and the new one twice. After the change every other device of this account signs out and asks for the new password; this phone stays signed in. A forgotten password cannot be recovered, so keep it somewhere safe. 16 Sign out on this device Takes this phone out of the account. It asks first. This phone leaves the account and forgets the sign-in. Resources attached from this server stay in the list and show as unavailable until you add the server again. If the server cannot be reached, a message says that the phone stays in the account's device list until another device revokes it. Undo The sign-in on this phone is forgotten. To come back, sign in again with the password or a pairing code; the account and its other devices are not touched. 17 Delete my account Deletes your account from the server for good. You enter the account password to confirm, and the window opens on the safe button. The server erases the account at once: all its devices, published folders and broadcasts, sign-ins and the clipboard. Folders you added stay in your list but show as no longer published. A button in the window opens a page of the project website on how it works. Undo This cannot be undone. The account, its device list and everything published through it are gone from the server; only signing up again with a new invitation brings back an account, and it starts empty. Devices of an account (tap a card) 18 Device list The devices that belong to this account, and whether each is online. A window titled with the server's address lists every device in the account: its name, the program it runs, and Online or Offline in words. This phone is shown as This phone. A device that has paused sharing is marked so. Close shuts the window. 19 Revoke Cuts a device off from the account. Every device except this phone has a Revoke button. It asks first and names the device. The device loses access and can come back only by signing in again. This phone has no such button; it leaves with Sign out on this device. Undo The device is removed from the account at once. To bring it back, sign in again on that device with the password or a pairing code. 20 Issue a pairing code Makes a one-time code for signing in another device. The code appears below the button together with the time it is valid until. Enter it on the other device instead of the password; it works once, so ask for a new one if it was not used. It is handy on a TV box or any device where typing a strong password is hard. Sign in to an exchange server window 21 Paste a server string Fills in the server from a connection string. Paste the text you were given, press Paste to take it from the clipboard, Scan QR to read a code with the camera, or Choose file to open a file of the kind the server makes. The string holds the server's address and the fingerprint of its certificate, never a login or a password, and it fills in what it can. If it is an invitation, the window turns into creating a new account: the password is asked twice and the button reads Create account. 22 Address (host:port) Where the server is, as host and port. Filled in by the connection string, or typed by hand as host:port. A wrong form is pointed out before anything is sent. Changing the address after reading a string drops the certificate that came with it. 23 Login Your login on that server. A login is 3 to 64 Latin letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores. It is only an account name; the server's owner gives it to you or you choose it when you accept an invitation. 24 Password Your password on that server. It is sent to the server once and not kept by the phone: the phone keeps a device sign-in instead. If you ticked the pairing code box, this field becomes the Pairing code field. 25 I have a pairing code instead of the password Lets you use a pairing code in place of the password. Tick it when another of your devices issued a one-time code. The Password field becomes Pairing code. The code works once and for a short time only. 26 Sign in Tries the sign-in. While the server answers, the window shows progress. If the server presents a certificate this phone does not know, a window asks you to check its fingerprint against the one the server shows and then Trust it or Cancel; do not trust a fingerprint that does not match. On success the window closes and the server appears as a card.
