pages.title: Help - Network Monitor
pages.description: A live view of your connections: Wi-Fi, mobile network, Bluetooth and satellites, with signal graphs and the details of the active link. It also holds checks you can run, such as speed, ping and a scan of your local network, and keeps a history of what you measured.
pages.body: Help index / Network Monitor Network Monitor What this is for A live view of your connections: Wi-Fi, mobile network, Bluetooth and satellites, with signal graphs and the details of the active link. It also holds checks you can run, such as speed, ping and a scan of your local network, and keeps a history of what you measured. In this order Start on the summary. The card at the top 1 says what you are connected to and whether the internet works; below it are your local address 2 , your external address 3 and the speed right now 4 . Each tile 5 opens one section. The line on a tile says in words whether the section works on this device, needs a permission, or has nothing to show, so you know before you open it. Wi-Fi 13 , mobile network 18 and Bluetooth 20 show what you are connected to, with a signal graph. Satellites 23 shows how many satellites the phone sees and where it thinks it is. Internet 27 draws the path from the phone to the internet and the traffic now. Pick what to check 29 , then check a resource, scan the local network, look up the external address or measure the speed. A notice 50 may come first. Tools 35 pings a host, traces its route and scans a range of addresses. Resource speed 42 measures the speed to one of your resources. Every check you run is kept in History 45 . Export it 46 to send the list to someone, or clear it 47 . If the screen says that Network Monitor is off, press 49 to open Settings and turn it on. The elements Summary 1 Active connection Tells you what you are connected to and whether it reaches the internet. The headline reads like Wi-Fi - MyNetwork - Internet works. The last part says whether the internet works, whether the network wants you to sign in, whether you are connected without internet, or whether you are offline. With nothing connected the card says so and suggests turning on Wi-Fi or mobile data. The readings are refreshed about once a second while this screen is open. 2 Local IP The address of your phone inside the network you are on. Tap the row to copy the address. The row is shown only while something is connected. If the phone has no address yet, it says Unknown. 3 External IP The address the internet sees for you, shown only when you ask. It stays hidden until you tap the row, because finding it means asking a public service on the internet. The row then says Asking.. and shows the address; tap it again to copy it. The address is kept only while the app runs and is never written to the history. The same lookup is under Internet, where it comes with a notice first. 4 Current speed How much data is flowing to and from this phone right now. Two figures: incoming with a down arrow and outgoing with an up arrow, counted for the whole phone, not just this app. It is a live reading, not a speed test; the graph is in the Internet section. The row is hidden while nothing is connected. 5 Wi-Fi Opens the Wi-Fi section. The tile shows the network name and the link speed when the phone knows them. Its status line says Available, or why not: Permission not granted, Nothing connected right now, or No such hardware on this device. Before the first reading it says Open to check. 6 Mobile Opens the mobile network section. The tile shows the name of the operator whose SIM is used for data. The status line works as on every tile. 7 Bluetooth Opens the Bluetooth section. The tile shows how many devices are connected right now, for example Connected now: 2. 8 Satellites Opens the satellites section. This tile uses the location receiver of the phone. If location is switched off in the system settings, the status line says so: Location is switched off in system settings. 9 Internet Opens the Internet section with the path, the traffic and the checks. Once you have looked up your external address in this session, the tile shows it. 10 History Opens the list of the measurements you ran. Checks you start from Internet, Tools and Resource speed end up here. 11 Tools Opens ping, traceroute and the subnet scan. These are for people who need to check a particular host or look at a local network. 12 Resource Speed Opens the speed test for one of your resources. It measures how fast files move to and from a network or cloud resource you added to the app. Wi-Fi, mobile network and Bluetooth 13 Wi-Fi radio Turns the Wi-Fi radio on or off. Android 10 and later usually do not let an app switch Wi-Fi by itself. When you tap the switch, the app tries, and if the system refuses it opens the system Wi-Fi panel instead; the switch moves when the panel changes the state. Where the device allows no switching at all, the switch is grayed out with a short explanation. If the state cannot be read it says State unknown. Tap the section heading to open the system Wi-Fi settings. 14 Network The network you are connected to, its frequency, link speed and Wi-Fi standard. The network name needs the precise location permission, because Android treats a Wi-Fi name as location data. Without it that row says Permission not granted. Tap to grant it, or Permission is blocked. Tap to open app settings, and the rest of the rows still work. When nothing is connected, the block is replaced by the reason. 15 Hotspot Shows whether your phone is sharing its connection as a hotspot. It reads Hotspot: On, Off or Not determined. Tap it to open the system hotspot settings. The row is hidden when the phone cannot tell. 16 Signal A graph of the Wi-Fi signal strength over the last minutes. One reading a second, in dBm; a value closer to 0 is a stronger signal. Under the graph you see now, lowest, highest and the trend: rising, falling or steady. Until the first readings arrive it says Collecting readings.. and the graph stays empty. It needs the precise location permission. Tap the graph to restart it and begin collecting from now. A screen reader announces the restart. 17 Link details The technical details of the active connection. Interface, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, DNS servers, gateway, whether there is a default route, a proxy and the bandwidth estimates for incoming and outgoing data. A missing value reads Unknown. Handy when you need to tell a support person what your network looks like. 18 SIM cards How many modems are active and which operator each SIM belongs to. The number of active modems needs no permission. The SIM rows show the operator of SIM 1 and SIM 2 and mark the one preferred for data; they need the phone permission, and without it the section says Permission not granted. Tap to grant it. Each SIM gets its own signal graph that you can restart by tapping it. 19 Open system network settings Opens the system screen where mobile data and SIMs are controlled. Android does not let an app switch mobile data or choose a SIM, and a note on the screen says so. This button takes you to the system network settings, where you can. 20 Bluetooth radio Turns the Bluetooth radio on or off. It works like the Wi-Fi switch: the app tries, and if the system refuses it opens the system Bluetooth settings. Tap the section heading to open them directly. The Adapter row says On, Off or Not on this device. 21 Connected now Lists the devices connected now and the ones only paired. Two lists: Connected now and Paired, not connected, each with a note when it is empty. Reading them needs the Bluetooth permission (Nearby devices on Android 12 and later); without it the lists say Permission not granted, and a tap asks for it. 22 Chart a connected device Chooses a connected device to draw its signal graph. The list offers the devices connected now. Once you pick one, a Device signal graph appears and fills in once a second; tap the graph to restart it. With no connected device the field says there is nothing to chart. Satellites and Internet 23 Satellites in view How many satellites the phone sees, and how many it uses to fix its position. Below the two counts is a line for each satellite: the system and number, the signal strength in dB-Hz, and whether it is counted in the position. A message says Searching for satellites.. until the first ones are found. A signal strength graph follows; tap it to restart. This section needs the precise location permission and location switched on. Tapping the heading or either count opens the system location settings. 24 Position Your coordinates, how accurate they are and when they were fixed. Latitude and longitude, the accuracy (for example ±5 m) and the time of the fix. Without a fix, or without the permission, the block gives the reason instead. The coordinates stay on the screen and are not sent anywhere. 25 Record the track on this device Records the path you move along while this screen is open. The track stays on this device and is written only while the screen is open. Nothing is sent anywhere. While it records, a line counts the recorded points. 26 Share the track file Sends the recorded track file to another app. The button appears once there is a track file. It opens the system share sheet with a CSV file. If a newer recording has replaced the file, a note asks you to turn recording on and try again. 27 Path to the internet Draws the way from your phone to the internet in four steps. This device, Gateway (your router), DNS and Internet, each with its address or state and a mark showing whether it answers. Where the line breaks is where to look: the router, the name servers or the connection beyond them. 28 Traffic on this device Shows the traffic of the whole phone, now and over the last minutes. Incoming now and Outgoing now, with a graph beneath. It counts everything the phone moves, not only this app. Tap the graph to restart it. 29 What to check Chooses what the checks below look at: the internet or one of your resources. The list starts with The internet and continues with the resources you added. Check the selected resource is available only when a resource is chosen. 30 Check the selected resource Checks whether the selected resource answers. It tries to reach the resource with its saved address and credentials and says The resource answered, or that it did not, so you check the address and credentials. If the resource was deleted meanwhile, the result says so. 31 Scan the local network Looks for devices on your local network and the ports they have open. Fill in the From and To addresses, or keep the range filled in for your own network. The result tells how many of the probed addresses answered and lists them with their open ports. A range that is too large or not a pair of addresses is refused with a hint. On newer Android versions the scan needs the local-network permission; if it is missing, the result tells you to grant it in the system settings and try again. The scan contacts addresses on your network. Some office and campus networks treat that as unwanted, so the app shows a notice the first time in a session. 32 Show the external address Asks a public service for the address the internet sees. The result shows the address and a note on whether it is your own or the operator translates it between its customers. If the router does not answer, the note says it can tell nothing either way. If no service answers, it says so and suggests trying again. The first time in a session a notice explains that the service sees the address it answers to. 33 Measure the speed Measures download and upload speed to the internet or to the chosen resource. The test downloads and uploads about 20 MB in total, so a notice appears first. On a network the phone knows as metered the notice appears every time, and without your approval nothing is measured. The result shows both speeds in Mbps. If the test cannot finish, the result asks you to check the connection. 34 Stop Stops the check that is running. It appears with a progress bar while a check runs. Stop it at any time; the other checks stay unavailable until the running one finishes or is stopped. Tools, resource speed and history 35 IP or host name The address or name of the host to ping or trace. Type an IP address or a host name. Below the field are chips with the hosts you used before: tap one to reuse it, tap its cross to forget it. 36 Ping Sends a few small requests to the host and reports how fast it answers. The console lists each attempt with its time in milliseconds, or No answer in time, and ends with how many of the attempts answered. A name that does not resolve or a missing network is reported in the console too. 37 Traceroute Shows the hops between your phone and the host. Each hop that answers is listed with its time. The trace ends when the host is reached or after the maximum number of hops. Use it to see where a connection slows down or stops. 38 Scan the local network Looks for devices that answer in an address range. It works like the scan in Internet, with the same From and To fields, and writes the answering addresses into the console. Use it only on networks that are yours. 39 Console output Shows the results of ping, traceroute and the scan as text. Before anything runs it says that results will appear here. While an operation runs, a progress bar with Stop appears above the console. 40 Copy Copies the console text to the clipboard. Use it to paste the results into a message or a note. With an empty console nothing is copied. 41 Clear Empties the console. Only the text on the screen is removed. The measurements already written to the history stay there. Undo The console text is lost with no way back. Copy it first if you need it. 42 Target Resource Chooses what to measure the speed to: the internet or one resource. The list starts with The internet and continues with the network and cloud resources you added. 43 Measure the speed Measures how fast data moves to and from the chosen target. It first checks that the target answers, then measures. A progress bar with Stop is shown while it runs. On a metered network a window asks first whether to go on. 44 Speed Results The download and upload speeds measured, in Mbps. Download and Upload, each in megabits per second. A resource that is read-only shows (Read-only resource) in place of the upload, because uploading would write to it. Under the figures a status line says that the measurement finished, was stopped, or why it failed. 45 History The measurements you ran, newest first. Each row has the kind (Speed, Resource check, External address, Network scan, Ping or Traceroute), the network it ran on, the time and whether it answered. The list is kept on this device. While it is empty the screen says there are no measurements yet. 46 Export Sends the whole list as a text file. It opens the system share sheet with a plain text file. If the file cannot be prepared, a note asks you to free some space. The button is shown only when the list has rows. 47 Clear Deletes every stored measurement. A window asks first. The button is shown only when the list has rows. Undo Every measurement is removed from the device and cannot be restored. Export the list first if you still need it. When Network Monitor is off 48 Network Monitor is off Tells you that Network Monitor is switched off in Settings. Instead of the sections you see a short message and, where the feature exists, a button. In some editions Network Monitor is not part of the app at all; the message then says so and has no button. The screen does not show the message while it is still checking whether the monitor is on. 49 Open settings Opens Settings on the tab where Network Monitor is switched on. It takes you to the Management tab, where the switch is under Additional programs and scenarios (the message on this screen calls it Operations). Turn it on, come back, and the summary appears. Notice and confirmation windows 50 Continue Goes ahead with the check after you have read the notice. The notice says what the check does: that the speed test uses about 20 MB of traffic, that the scan contacts your local network, that the external address lookup is passed to a public service, or that this network charges for traffic. The traffic, scan and address notices come once per session; the metered notice comes before every speed test. 51 Cancel Closes the notice and does not run the check. Nothing is sent and nothing is measured. 52 Clear Confirms that you want to clear the measurement history. The window says the stored measurements will be removed from this device and suggests exporting first. Undo The measurements are deleted for good. Export them before you confirm if you may need them. 53 Cancel Closes the window and keeps the history. Nothing is deleted. pages.title: Help - Player
pages.description: The player opens a file from the file browser: it plays a video or music, shows a photo, and reads a document, a book or a text. The same screen has the buttons to move on to another file, to file the one you are on and to share it.
pages.body: Help index / Player Player What this is for The player opens a file from the file browser: it plays a video or music, shows a photo, and reads a document, a book or a text. The same screen has the buttons to move on to another file, to file the one you are on and to share it. In this order Open a file from the file browser. A video starts in full screen: tap the picture to bring the buttons back, and use Fullscreen 13 to switch between the picture alone and the picture with the command panel. Play/Pause 19 starts and stops playback; Rewind 18 and Forward 20 jump 10 seconds, and the seek bar 15 takes you to any moment. Previous file 17 and Next file 21 walk through the folder in the order of the file browser; a swipe left or right on the picture does the same. Random 3 jumps to any file. Playback order 16 chooses what happens when a file ends: repeat one, loop the list, play through or shuffle. Playback settings 22 holds speed, volume, soundtrack, subtitles and colors. Rename 9 , Edit 10 , Delete 11 and Share 7 act on the file you are on, Undo 12 takes back a delete or a move, and Favorite 6 adds the file to your favorites. More actions 14 opens the menu with everything else for this kind of file, such as save a frame, rotate, cast or translate. Picture in picture 23 shrinks a video into a small window, and Help in the menu or F1 opens this page. The elements Command panel 1 Back Closes the player and returns to the file list. The Back button of the device does the same. A tap in the top left corner of the picture does it too. 2 Previous Goes to the previous file of the folder. It follows the order of the file browser. A file you deleted or moved is already gone from the list, so Previous never lands on it. 3 Random Jump Jumps to a random file of the folder. Handy for a mixed listen or a quick look at something you forgot you had. 4 Next Goes to the next file of the folder. It follows the order of the file browser. A swipe left on a photo or video does the same. 5 Slideshow Starts and stops the slideshow. In a slideshow the player moves to the next file by itself. The pace and the look are set in Settings, on the Media tab. 6 Favorite Adds the file to your favorites, or takes it out. Everything you mark is gathered in Favorites on the main screen. 7 Share Sends the file to another app or person. A file from a network or cloud folder is fetched as a temporary copy first. 8 File Information Shows what the app knows about the file. Size, full path and, where they apply, resolution or camera settings. 9 Rename Renames the file you are on. A dialog asks for the new name. 10 Edit Opens the editing tools for the file you are on. What opens depends on the kind of file: the playback settings for a video or music, the editing window for a photo, a GIF or a PDF. 11 Delete Deletes the file you are on, after you confirm. A deleted file leaves the list at once. Undo Undo brings the file back for as long as the app still remembers the operation. 12 Undo Takes back the last delete or move. The button appears right after such an operation. 13 Fullscreen mode Hides the command panel so only the picture is left. To get the panel back, tap the picture or the Exit fullscreen button that stays in the corner. Turning the phone sideways goes full screen by itself, and turning it back upright brings the panel back. A video keeps playing through both. 14 More actions Opens the menu with the rest of the actions. Buttons that did not fit move here, so nothing disappears. The menu depends on the kind of file: save a frame of a video, rotate or crop a photo, search, translate and extract text in a document or a book, lyrics and sleep timer for music, cast, print and Send to. The F1 key opens this page; so does Help in this menu. Playback 15 Seek bar Shows how far the file has played and lets you jump to any moment. Drag the knob or tap on the bar. The time played and the length of the file stand on both sides of it. 16 Playback order Chooses what happens when a file ends. Repeat one plays the same file over and over. Loop list goes back to the first file after the last. Play through stops after the last file. Shuffle plays in a random order. 17 Previous file Goes to the previous file of the folder. The same as Previous on the command panel, close to the thumb. 18 Rewind 10 seconds Jumps 10 seconds back. Press it several times to go back further. 19 Play/Pause Starts and pauses playback. For an animated picture such as a GIF it plays and stops the animation. The player remembers how far you watched, so the same file continues from there next time. 20 Fast forward 10 seconds Jumps 10 seconds ahead. Press it several times to skip a long intro. 21 Next file Goes to the next file of the folder. The same as Next on the command panel, close to the thumb. 22 Playback settings Opens the window with the playback settings. Speed, including very slow 0.1x and 0.3x, volume, brightness, soundtrack, subtitles and colors. In portrait the sliders stand upright, so a thumb moves them from bottom to top. 23 Picture in Picture Shrinks the video into a small window above other apps. The button is shown for a video when the device supports it. pages.title: Help - Edit Resource
pages.description: Edit Resource changes a resource you already added: its name and icon, the address or path it points to, which files it shows and how it behaves. Open it from the main screen by holding a resource or with the edit button in its row. The same screen sets up a new internet stream and saves a copy of a resource.
headings: What the resource shows and how it behaves
pages.body: Help index / Edit Resource Edit Resource What this is for Edit Resource changes a resource you already added: its name and icon, the address or path it points to, which files it shows and how it behaves. Open it from the main screen by holding a resource or with the edit button in its row. The same screen sets up a new internet stream and saves a copy of a resource. In this order Start with the name 6 . Names must be unique: if yours is taken, the app says so and offers Use suggested name 7 . Open Connection Settings 8 to correct the path, the address and port, the sign-in or the stream address. For a network or cloud resource, check the new values with Test Connection 9 ; Retry 10 repeats the last action after a failure. Decide what the resource shows: Content Scanning Conditions 11 and the file types in Media Types 12 . Resource Profile 13 fills in a ready set in one tap. Use Destination Settings 14 to use the resource for Quick Sort or to make it read-only, and Advanced Settings 15 for a comment, a PIN and the slideshow interval. Pick an icon 3 if you want the resource to stand out in the list. Press Save Changes 5 ; it stays off until something valid has changed. Save as Copy 4 keeps the original and stores your edits as a new resource, and Reset Changes 2 brings back the saved values. Statistics 16 tell you when the resource was created and opened, and Add to Home Screen 17 puts a shortcut to it on your home screen. The elements Toolbar and actions 1 Back Closes the editor without saving your changes. The arrow in the toolbar, the Back button of the device and the Esc key all leave the screen at once. Nothing is saved on the way out, so press Save Changes first if you want to keep your edits. Shortcut Esc 2 Reset Changes Puts every field back to the values saved with the resource. The button shows up only after you change something. It restores all fields, the icon and the profile to how they were when the editor opened, and clears the last connection test result. Undo Your edits since opening the editor are lost and cannot be brought back. Saved values are not touched. 3 Pick resource icon Chooses the picture that stands for this resource in lists. Opens the Choose an icon sheet; the button itself shows the icon the resource has now. The new icon is stored when you press Save Changes. If you change the profile and have not chosen an icon by hand in this session, the icon follows the profile on its own. 4 Save as Copy Stores your edits as a new resource and leaves the original as it is. Available when you edit an existing resource. The copy gets a free name based on the original one, and the editor stays on the original afterwards. It is greyed out while the form has errors or a test or save is running. 5 Save Changes Saves your changes to the resource. The button is off until the form is valid and something has actually changed. After saving you see Resource saved successfully and the screen closes. Ctrl+S does the same as the button; if there is nothing to save, a short note says so. Shortcut Ctrl + S Name and connection 6 Resource Name The name the resource has in your lists. Names are compared without regard to upper and lower case, so Photos and photos count as the same. When the name is already in use, a red note says so and the suggestions appear below; the name of the resource you are editing is never treated as a duplicate of itself. 7 Use suggested name Replaces a taken name with the first suggestion. The button appears only when the name you typed is already used by another resource. Its text carries the suggested name, and one tap puts it into the field. 8 Connection Settings Where the resource points to: a folder, a server, a cloud folder or a stream. A collapsible section whose fields depend on the type. A local resource shows Folder Path. A network resource shows Host / IP Address, Port, Username, Password and Server Path (optional). A cloud resource shows Cloud Folder ID, and a stream shows its URL (http, https, rtsp). Collections such as Recent Media have no path, so the section is not shown for them. After you change the path, the address or the port, a warning says that a rescan or re-check is needed. While a password field is on screen, the screen can be hidden from screenshots and the recent apps view, depending on the Secure sensitive screens setting. 9 Test Connection Checks the connection settings before you save them. Shown for network and cloud resources. The app first checks that the form is filled in correctly, then connects and shows the result in a coloured line: green for success, with a count of what it found, a warning colour for a partial result and red for a failure. Nothing is saved by the test. 10 Retry Repeats the last action after a failure. The button appears under a failed connection test. It runs again whatever you did last: the test, Save Changes or Save as Copy. What the resource shows and how it behaves 11 Content Scanning Conditions Decides which files of the resource the app looks at. A collapsible section. Scan subdirectories looks for media in nested folders, and Show subfolders as items needs it. All Files mode lets you browse and manage every file, not only media; Show hidden files needs it. Disable thumbnails shows extension icons instead of previews, and Remember file list keeps a copy of the list for faster opening. Only the choices that fit the resource type are shown. 12 Media Types Chooses which kinds of files the resource shows. Tick Videos, Audio, Images, GIFs, Text, PDF, EPUB and Office documents. The boxes are locked while All Files mode is on. The section does not appear for resources that have no file types, such as a stream. 13 Resource Profile Applies a ready set of media settings in one tap. The button shows the current profile and opens Resource Profile: Custom, Audio Library, Video Library, Photo Storage, Documents and File Manager Mode. A profile sets the media types, All Files mode and, for Audio Library, Remember file list at once. Custom changes nothing, so use the checkboxes to tune by hand afterwards. 14 Destination Settings Marks the resource for Quick Sort and can make it read-only. Use as destination folder puts the resource on your Quick Sort list so you can send files to it. Read-only mode blocks copy, move and delete in it. Both together is a bad mix, because a read-only place cannot receive files, so a warning appears. 15 Advanced Settings Optional extras: a comment, a PIN and the slideshow interval. Comment is a note for yourself. PIN Code (4-6 digits) protects the resource: the app asks for it before it opens the editor again, among other things. Slideshow Interval sets the seconds between pictures when this resource is played as a slideshow. Only the fields that fit the resource type are shown. Information 16 Statistics Facts about the resource: size, dates and speed. Shown only while you edit an existing resource. It lists the number of files and subfolders, when the resource was created and last opened, for network resources the last sync, and the read and write speed once they have been measured. A successful connection test refreshes the numbers. 17 Add to Home Screen Puts a shortcut to this resource on your home screen. The shortcut uses the same icon as the editor shows. Android asks you to confirm it. If your launcher cannot place shortcuts, a message says so. The button sits inside the Statistics section. 18 Warning note A short reminder that appears when your edits need attention. It can say that a read-only place cannot be a destination, that a changed path or address needs a rescan, or that another resource already has the same path. Each warning also opens in a window once, and the note stays until the cause is gone. Choose an icon (icon picker) 19 Icon set tabs Switches between the icon sets: Music, Video, Image, Documents and Other. The sheet opens on the set that suits your resource, based on its profile and type. Swipe the tab strip sideways if it does not fit the screen. 20 Icons Tapping an icon chooses it at once. The icon in use is marked with a ring. One tap on another icon closes the sheet and puts it on the button in the editor; it is stored when you press Save Changes. To leave without a change, swipe the sheet down. pages.title: Help - Scheduled file operations
pages.description: Scheduled file operations copy, move, archive or delete files in the background at the times you set - for example, moving new camera photos to a network folder every night. This screen switches the feature on, lists your operations and shows how every run went.
pages.body: Help index / Scheduled file operations Scheduled file operations What this is for Scheduled file operations copy, move, archive or delete files in the background at the times you set - for example, moving new camera photos to a network folder every night. This screen switches the feature on, lists your operations and shows how every run went. In this order Turn on Use scheduled operations 2 . On Android 13 and later, press the notifications button 3 if it shows up, so you can see when a run starts or fails. Press Add 4 and describe the job once: the source, the operation, the destination, which files to take, when to start and how often. Try a new job as Copy before you trust it with Move or Delete. Find the new card in the list 11 . Its own switch 12 holds just that job without deleting it. Not sure it works? Press Run now 15 on the card, then open its History 14 to see what was done. A warning mark 13 means the last run failed or was skipped. History 7 shows the log of all runs, the card's History 14 the runs of one job. To hold everything for a while use Pause all 6 . Run all now 5 starts every enabled job once, outside the schedule. Edit 16 changes a job, Delete 17 removes one, and Clear all 8 removes them all. Clear log 10 empties the run history and leaves the jobs alone. The elements Switch and help 1 Help Opens help for this screen. You get what each button does and the usual order of use, with numbers matching the markers on the screenshot. 2 Use scheduled operations Turns scheduled runs on or off for the whole program. While it is on, your operations run at their times, even when the app is closed. While it is off, nothing runs on schedule and the buttons and the list are hidden, but every operation stays saved. The switch also follows the list: it turns itself off when you delete the last operation and on again when you add one. Undo Nothing is lost. The operations stay saved, and switching it on queues their runs again. 3 Allow notifications for scheduled operations Lets scheduled runs show their notifications. The button appears on Android 13 and later while the notification permission is missing, and goes away once you allow it. A run shows a notification while it works and when it fails, so without the permission you would notice neither. Tap it and answer the system question. The warning mark on an operation card shows a failed run either way. Action bar 4 Add Creates a new scheduled operation. A form opens where you describe the job once. Source is one of your resources or any folder on the device. Operation is Copy, Move, Archive or Delete, and everything except Delete also asks for a Destination. Then pick the file types, optionally a time filter such as only files that are new since the last run, extra limits by name, age or size, the start time and how often to repeat (at least every 15 minutes). A read-only source allows Copy only. Save operation puts the new card in the list. When you arrive from the file browser, the form opens with the folder you were in already set as the source. Move and Delete remove the original files in the background, which on some devices needs access to all files; the app tells you in a notification when it is missing. 5 Run all now Starts every enabled operation once, right now. The jobs run one after another and the regular schedule goes on as before. Operations whose own switch is off are skipped, and nothing happens while Pause all is active. There is no extra question, so make sure a Move or Delete job is really ready before you press it. Undo Files that a run copied, moved or deleted stay that way. A scheduled Delete does not use the trash - what it removes is gone for good. 6 Pause all Holds all schedules, or lets them go on. While the schedules are paused the button reads Resume all. Pausing keeps every operation and its settings, makes Run all now do nothing, and keeps the app from queuing the schedules again after a restart. Resume all lifts the pause. To hold a single job, use the switch on its card. 7 History Shows or hides the log of all runs. The Run history panel opens under the buttons with the newest runs first: when each run happened, which operation it was, from where to where, and what came of it. Failures are shown in the error color. Press the button again to hide the panel. 8 Clear all Removes every scheduled operation at once. The app asks Clear all scheduled operations? first. After you confirm, all operations are deleted and their schedules cancelled. Your files are not touched, and the log in the Run history panel stays. With the list empty, the main switch turns itself off. Undo The operations and their settings are lost and cannot be restored - create them again with Add. Files that earlier runs already copied, moved or deleted stay as they are. Run history 9 Run history The log of recent runs, newest first. Each entry shows the time, the operation, the source and the destination, and a short message. The panel keeps the last 200 entries in view. Until a run is recorded it says No runs recorded yet. It is one list for all operations; for one operation use the History button on its card. 10 Clear log Empties the log of all runs. The app asks Clear the run history? first. After you confirm, the list is empty and fills up again with the next runs. Operations and schedules are not affected, and the runs shown by the card History buttons are kept. Undo The deleted log entries cannot be brought back. Only the entries are lost; nothing else changes. Operation list 11 Operation list One card for each scheduled operation. A card shows the source and, except for Delete, the destination, with an icon for the operation. Below are the schedule (for example At 23:00 · Every 24h), which files it takes, and when it last succeeded or that no run has succeeded yet. A source or destination that was removed from the app is shown as (deleted). While the list is empty it says No scheduled operations yet. Tap + to create the first one. 12 Enable/disable scheduled operation Holds or resumes this one operation. Off, the operation keeps its card and settings but its waiting run is cancelled. On, it is queued for its next time again. The other operations are not affected. 13 Warning mark Tells you the last run of this operation did not finish. It appears after a run that failed or was skipped, for example because the source or the destination could not be reached. A skipped run is tried again at the next time. The mark stays until a run succeeds; open the card History to see why. 14 History Shows the recent runs of this operation only. A window lists the runs of this one job, newest first: when each ran, how many files it handled and why it stopped, if it did. Close it with Close. The runs go away together with the operation. 15 Run now Starts this operation once, right now. Use it to try a new job or to catch up without waiting for the next time. The regular schedule is not changed. When it is done, the result appears in History. Undo The same as for any run: copied, moved or deleted files stay that way, and Delete is permanent. 16 Edit Changes the source, destination, files or times of this operation. The same form as Add opens with the current settings. Save operation keeps your changes; closing the form without saving leaves the operation as it was. 17 Delete Removes this operation. The app asks Delete this scheduled operation? first. After you confirm, the operation and its schedule are removed, together with its own run list and a folder that was chosen only for this job. Your files are not touched. Undo The operation cannot be restored - create it again with Add. Files that earlier runs already copied, moved or deleted stay as they are. Top bar menu 18 About schedules for other devices Opens a web page about schedules that work with folders of other devices. The item is in the three-dots menu of the top bar. It opens a page of the product website in your browser, so it needs an internet connection; the app tells you if the phone is offline or has no browser. The page explains how a schedule can take files from, or put them into, a folder on another device. pages.title: Help - Main screen
pages.description: The main screen lists your resources - the device folders, network shares and cloud folders you added. Add a resource, open it to browse its files, or start playback straight from here.
pages.body: Help index / Main screen Main screen What this is for The main screen lists your resources - the device folders, network shares and cloud folders you added. Add a resource, open it to browse its files, or start playback straight from here. In this order Press Add 2 to connect your first resource: a device folder, a network share or a cloud folder. Until you do, the list stays empty. If you use network or cloud resources, pick a kind with the tabs 12 to see only those. The tabs show up once a remote source is turned on. Tap a row in the list 13 to open its files in the file browser. Tap the row's icon to start a slideshow right away. Use Filter 3 to sort the list or narrow it down by kind or name. Refresh 4 comes in handy after files change outside the app. Switch the view with 7 when you want more or fewer resources on screen: list, grid or table. Run player 9 skips the browsing and starts the selected or most recent resource. Favorites 8 opens everything you starred. Settings 6 is where you tune the app, Help 11 opens this page, and Exit 1 leaves the app. The elements Command bar 1 Exit Leaves the app, or sends it to the background while something still runs. When music is playing, a recording is running, scheduled operations are working or edge gestures are on, one press only minimizes the app so those keep going, and the icon changes to show it. With nothing running in the background, one press closes the app. A long press always closes everything, background functions included. 2 Add Opens the screen where you add a new resource. A resource is a place with your files, such as a device folder, a network share or a cloud folder. Once you save it, it appears in the list and you can open it. Tapping the empty list does the same thing. 3 Filter Sorts the resource list and narrows it down. Pick a sort order (manual, name, date or number of files), then limit the list by resource type, media type or part of the name. The check mark applies your choice, and the clear-filters button resets it. While a filter is on, a note at the bottom of the list says which one. 4 Refresh Rescans every resource for new and changed files. Use it after copying files in from another app or a computer, or when a network share was offline. It also resets network connections and gives video thumbnails that failed earlier another try. 5 More actions Opens the menu with the actions that are not on the bar. The button shows up only when there is something in the menu: programs (when the programs panel is off), buttons that did not fit on a narrow screen, and Help. Nothing disappears on a small screen - it moves here. 6 Settings Opens the app settings, split into four tabs. The tabs are General, Media, Player and Management. Start with General for language, theme and device profile. If you are not sure where an option lives, Settings has a search. 7 Grid view / list view Switches how resources are shown: list, grid or table. The icon shows the view you get next, and your choice is remembered. The table needs a wide window - a tablet, desktop mode or a large unfolded screen - and adds columns for name, source, files, content and path, plus a details panel. Narrower windows switch between list and grid. 8 Favorites Opens everything you marked as a favorite, in one place. It opens Favorites in the file browser. The button is shown when Favorites is turned on in Settings; you mark files while you browse. 9 Run player Starts playback of a resource without opening the file browser. It plays the resource you selected. With no selection it takes the one you used last, or the first in the list. The button is grayed out while the list is empty. 10 Search resources Finds a resource by name or path in the table. The field appears only while the table view is on. Type a few letters and the rows narrow down as you go. Clear it to bring the whole list back. 11 Help Opens help for this screen. You get what each button does and the usual order of use, with numbers matching the markers on the screenshot. Resources 12 Resource type filter Shows only the resources of one kind. ALL shows everything; Local, SMB, S/FTP and Cloud keep just that kind. A tab is built only for a source you turned on, and the whole strip stays hidden until at least one network or cloud source is on, because Local would show the same as ALL. Long-press a tab to fold the strip into a small chip, and tap the chip to bring it back. 13 Resources Your resources, one row or tile each. Tap a row to open its files in the file browser. Tap its icon to start a slideshow, or press and hold the row to edit the resource. Each row also has buttons to edit, copy its settings, move it up or down, delete it or open more actions. Undo Deleting a resource asks first, removes it from the app and cancels scheduled operations that use it. Your files stay where they are, and you can add the resource again. pages.body: Wear OS Watch FastMedia Wear Watch Recipe #12 The full version of the watch app (sideload only). Pins made on the phone and channels sent from the phone need the phone app in the Standard or noLegal edition. Streaming Radio and TV on Your Wrist - Finding, Pinning and Playing Live Channels Open the watch's own Streams screen, narrow thousands of live channels down with search, filters and sorting, pin the few you love, and play them on the watch alone - jumping back to the live moment after a pause. Why You'll Love This Internet radio is the perfect thing for a watch: no files to copy, no storage to fill, just a station and your headphones. The watch has its own catalog of live channels - radio and TV from all over the world - and plays them over Wi-Fi or mobile data without the phone. The catch is size: many thousands of channels on a screen that shows four at a time. This recipe shows how to get from that to the two or three you actually listen to, in a couple of taps. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites The watch app installed and paired - see installing and pairing the watch . The full version of the watch app. *Sideload version only* - see the noLegal edition . A watch with Wi-Fi or mobile data, and headphones or a speaker on the watch. Optional: the phone app with the Wear Companion switched on, to bring your phone's pinned channels and your own channels over. 1 Open Streams and let the catalog load On the watch's home screen, tap Streams . The first time, the list is still being put together - the watch shows it loading until the catalog is ready, rather than flashing an empty screen at you. If the catalog was never downloaded, tap Refresh catalog ; while it works you'll see Updating streams.. , and if the network lets you down, Could not update streams. Check your connection and try again . Don't see Streams on the home screen at all? Switch on Show Streams in the watch's settings. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Streams Round watch, Streams screen, toolbar with search, filter and sort, two-line counter, channel list. Profile: watch ID: wear.streams-list 2 Narrow thousands of channels down to a few Three small buttons sit at the top: Search streams , Filter streams and Sort streams . They stay pinned in place while the channel list scrolls under them, and the first channel is never hidden behind them. Beside them, two small lines count the channels: how many your search and filters leave, over the size of the whole catalog. Search - type or speak part of a channel's name. Filter - first choose what kind of channel you want: Video , Audio or Own (channels you sent over from the phone). Tap the lit choice again to see everything. Below that, pick a Topic , a Language or one of the Collections . Topics and languages are shown in your own language, with the busiest ones first and the number of channels on each, and the chips wrap onto new lines so every name is readable. Sort - Most used (the default: channels you actually play on the watch rise to the top), Name (A-Z) , Name (Z-A) or By media type . The watch remembers your filter and sort order when you leave the screen, restart the app or even reboot the watch. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Filter streams Round watch, Filter streams screen, Video Audio Own rows, Topic chips with counts wrapping onto several lines. Profile: watch ID: wear.streams-filter-sheet 3 When the filter leaves nothing Narrow things too far and the list says so honestly: No streams match the filter. Clear it to see the whole catalog. One tap on Clear filters removes every narrowing at once - kind, topic, language and collection - and your channels are back. This is different from an empty catalog. Downloading the catalog again wouldn't help here, so the watch doesn't suggest it. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: No matches Round watch, Streams screen, filtered-empty message and Clear filters chip. Profile: watch ID: wear.streams-filtered-empty 4 Play a channel Tap a channel. A radio station opens in the audio player , a TV channel in the video player . For the time a stream plays, the watch asks for a fast network connection and lets it go again afterwards, so it doesn't drain the battery when you stop. If the connection can't carry the stream, the watch tells you why instead of just going quiet: Connection too slow for this stream. Move closer to Wi-Fi and try again. Watch is offline. Reconnect, then try again. Connection not verified yet. Playback may stop - try again if it does. If a station stops sending altogether, the watch stops playback to save the battery and says The stream stopped sending. Playback was stopped to save the battery. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Connection too slow Round watch, stream player, message about a connection too slow for the stream. Profile: watch ID: wear.stream-connection-slow 5 The station line, and jumping back to live A live stream has no beginning and no end, so where a song would show its seek bar and running time, the audio player shows the station's own details instead: its name, genre, the audio format and the bitrate, such as 128 kbps . No bar you can't drag, no clock stuck at 0:00. Paused for a phone call? When you press play again you'd normally hear the broadcast from where you left off, a few minutes behind everyone else. Tap Jump to live - right after the play and pause button - and the watch reconnects and plays what's on air at this moment. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Live station Round watch, audio player on a live radio stream, station line with name, genre, codec and bitrate, Jump to live button. Profile: watch ID: wear.stream-station-line 6 Pin the channels you love While a channel plays, tap the pin in the player - Pin stream . The pin fills in, and from now on the channel sits at the top of the Streams list. Tap it again - Unpin stream - to let it go. The pin remembers the channel by its address, so it survives a fresh download of the catalog. Channels you pinned on the phone come over to the watch too. The list then has three groups: channels pinned on the watch first, channels pinned only on the phone next, and everything else after them, each group in the sort order you chose. A channel pinned on both devices appears once, among the watch's own. Unpin a channel on the phone and it leaves the watch's phone group; a pin you made on the watch stays. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Pin stream Round watch, stream player, filled pin button after Pin stream. Profile: watch ID: wear.stream-pin-button What You Get From a catalog of thousands you're down to a handful of pinned channels at the top of the list, playing on the watch alone, and always one tap away from the live moment. Tips and Troubleshooting Your own channels from the phone are in the Own filter - send one over with Send to watch on the phone, as described in streams on a TV, a watch or a VR headset . Most used learns as you go - after a few days, the stations you really listen to rise to the top on their own. Pin on the phone, listen on the watch - pins you make in the phone's Streams show up on the watch automatically.
